citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes what ice protection prevents but does not state the aerodynamic/air-data consequence of accretion, which is needed to derive the class.

assumptions.text: Shared bleed/heating demand reduces available ice-protection capacity to a degree that is a significant but not large margin reduction.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the shared-demand shortfall is larger than assumed, SF-016-PL2 could rise to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016-PL2 (Major)

citations.quote: a bleed demand to the environmental system that reduces pack capacity when in use

assumptions.rationale: The SDD notes ice protection reduces pack capacity when in use but does not quantify the resulting protection shortfall, forcing a judgement on the class.

assumptions.text: Erroneous/asymmetric activation produces an asymmetric accretion condition that is a significant handling-margin reduction rather than a large one.
assumptions.ifWrong: If worst-case asymmetric accretion is more severe, SF-016-M could rise to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016-M (Major)

citations.quote: erroneous or asymmetric ice-protection activation

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM names the malfunction but the SDD does not state the handling consequence of asymmetric accretion, forcing the severity judgement.

assumptions.text: The heated probes protected by SF-017 include the pitot, static and angle-of-attack sensing that feed the primary and standby air-data systems.
assumptions.ifWrong: If probe heating does not cover air-data probes, SF-017-M/M2/TL lose their air-data-integrity effect and would likely drop below Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-M, SF-017-M2, SF-017-TL severity

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually

assumptions.rationale: The AFHA function is stated as 'Heat probes and detect icing' but the aircraft function list does not enumerate which probes; the air-data effect that drives severity was inferred from the AVI system description.

assumptions.text: The two installed ice detectors are of the same type, so masked/failed detection cannot be assumed independent between channels for common-mode credit.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the detectors are shown independent, the masked/failed-detection likelihood credit improves but the stated Hazardous effect (undetected accretion) is unchanged; the CMA disposition still gates confirmation.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-M, SF-017-M2 severity and their CMA note

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records detector commonality as an item for examination but does not resolve it; the classification of masked/failed detection depends on whether the detection credit survives a common-mode fault.

assumptions.text: An independent standby air-data path survives the complete loss of probe heating well enough to hold SF-017-TL at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no usable independent air-data source survives, SF-017-TL could escalate toward Catastrophic and require Extremely Improbable objective.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-TL severity

citations.quote: Standby attitude, airspeed and altitude are provided by an independent integrated standby instrument

assumptions.rationale: The residual air-data capability after total probe-heat loss is not quantified in the provided material; the standby instrument is described but its sensing independence from heated probes is not confirmed.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effects for all SF-017 conditions are limited to the flight crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, occupant-effect statements and possibly severity for the icing conditions would need revisiting.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax for SF-017-M, SF-017-M2, SF-017-PL, SF-017-PL2, SF-017-TL

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Occupant-effect field requires knowing who is aboard; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight and crew are the only occupants.

assumptions.text: The standby instrument is genuinely independent of the primary displays in supply, sensing and processing, and is adequate to continue flight and complete an approach to the semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby is not adequate or shares a common source with the primaries, SF-018-TL escalates from Hazardous (HAZ-1) toward Catastrophic (CAT-1).
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-TL severity

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The complete-loss (TL) severity of Hazardous rather than Catastrophic rests entirely on a surviving independent standby means; the provided material asserts independence but not its adequacy across all phases.

assumptions.text: Erroneous/misleading information can be presented to the crew as valid without an independent, timely cue that flags it as wrong.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a reliable independent monitor always flags misleading data in time for crew action, SF-018-M / SF-018-M2 may reduce below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M and SF-018-M2 severity

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: The Catastrophic proposal for SF-018-M and SF-018-M2 depends on the misleading data being undetectable in time; the provided material does not state a comparison/monitor that would guarantee detection of agreed-wrong display data.

assumptions.text: SF-018-M2 and SF-018-PL2 are the navigation and standby-only sub-cases of the broader SF-018-M and SF-018-PL FCIM entries respectively, rather than separately maintained FCIM conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If they are intended as independent conditions with different content, their effects and classifications may differ from the SF-018-M / SF-018-PL parents.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M2 and SF-018-PL2 rows
assumptions.rationale: SF-018-M2 and SF-018-PL2 are named in this turn but do not appear as distinct entries in the FCIM; their scope was inferred from the descriptions provided in the turn.

assumptions.text: Crew alerting is the crew's primary and consolidated means of learning of system failures and the required response.
assumptions.ifWrong: If independent per-system annunciations exist outside the alerting system, the effects (and any eventual severity) of SF-019-M2 and SF-019-PL2 reduce because failures would still be indicated by another means.

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a single consolidated alert list but the AFHA has no other function stating an independent crew-notification path; severity of every SF-019 malfunction/loss row leans on how much the crew depends on alerting.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so there are no passengers to suffer effects.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, the effect-on-passengers field and possibly the driving severity would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all SF-019 rows

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Effect-on-occupants field requires knowing occupancy; the SDD states crew-only operation.

assumptions.text: The two alerting processing channels are independent such that partial loss (SF-019-PL) leaves alerting available on the surviving channel and the degraded state is itself annunciated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a channel loss is not self-annunciated or defeats coverage, SF-019-PL effect worsens toward the SF-019-PL2 / M2 case and its eventual severity rises.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-PL

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: SF-019-PL severity direction depends on retained coverage and self-annunciation; the SDD states two independent channels but does not state fault-annunciation of a lost channel.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so no passenger-occupant effects apply to any of these conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold were occupied in flight, the passenger effect and possibly the severity of SF-020-M2 (undetected hold fire) would worsen.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-019-TL, SF-020-M, SF-020-M2, SF-020-PL, SF-020-PL2

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The function definitions do not state occupancy; the aircraft/crew/pax effect columns require an occupancy premise to fill the passenger column.

assumptions.text: An undetected fire in a monitored fire zone can propagate to loss of the airplane because the hold carries no suppression and engine/APU response depends on crew action following annunciation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an independent means arrests an undetected fire, SF-020-M2 and the masked half of SF-020-M would classify below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: severity of SF-020-M2; severityRationale of SF-020-M

citations.quote: The hold has smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression

assumptions.rationale: The aircraft-function statement names detection only; deriving the Catastrophic effect for SF-020-M2 requires the design fact that suppression/response depends on detection and that the hold has none.

assumptions.text: Crew alerting is the single consolidated, prioritised means by which the crew learns of system failures and their procedures.
assumptions.ifWrong: If independent per-system indication fully substitutes for the consolidated list, SF-019-TL severity would reduce below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: severity of SF-019-TL

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.rationale: The severity of SF-019-TL depends on whether an equivalent alternative alerting path exists; the function definition does not describe redundancy at aircraft level.

assumptions.text: An undetected or unsuppressed fire in an engine nacelle, APU compartment or bleed/gear-bay fire zone can progress to structural damage before crew intervention.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-020-TL severity could drop below Hazardous, or rise toward Catastrophic if uncontrolled nacelle fire threatens the airframe.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-TL, SF-021-M, SF-021-PL severities

citations.quote: Each engine nacelle and the APU compartment carry dual-loop continuous fire detection

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes detection and suppression provisions but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an undetected/uncontrolled fire, which is needed to derive severity.

assumptions.text: SF-021-M2 (agent to the wrong nacelle) is a distinct intended failure condition even though the current FCIM carries SF-021-M as the mis-routing case.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-021-M2 row should be dropped as a duplicate of SF-021-M rather than left as an unclassified row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021-M2 row
assumptions.rationale: The turn instruction lists SF-021-M2 but the project FCIM does not contain it; provenance is the requested list, not the model.

assumptions.text: The engine fire-extinguisher architecture provides two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, so loss of one bottle leaves single-shot redundancy for the pair.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no residual bottle remains after the inadvertent/partial event, SF-021-M and SF-021-PL could escalate to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021-M, SF-021-PL severities

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed

assumptions.rationale: Severity of SF-021-M and SF-021-PL depends on residual suppression capability, taken from the SDD's stated bottle count and cross-plumbing.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so occupant effects are limited to the airframe consequence.
assumptions.ifWrong: Passenger/occupant effects and severities would need re-evaluation if the hold or additional occupants are present.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all five rows

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Occupant-effect fields depend on there being no passengers/hold occupants in flight.

assumptions.text: The aircraft hold is unoccupied in flight and only flight crew are carried, so all passenger-effect fields are not applicable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, the occupant-effect column and potentially the severity of the oxygen and fire conditions would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all five rows (SF-021-PL2, SF-021-TL, SF-022-M, SF-022-PL, SF-022-PL2)

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA requires an occupant effect for each condition; the SDD must be relied on to establish there are no passengers.

assumptions.text: Either crew oxygen cylinder alone can supply the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve via the crossover, so venting one cylinder retains the function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single cylinder cannot cover the required diversion duration, SF-022-M would no longer be a slight reduction and its severity would rise.
assumptions.usedFor: severity=Minor (MIN-1) on SF-022-M

citations.quote: Two cylinders with a crossover, either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve

assumptions.rationale: The Minor classification of SF-022-M rests on the surviving-cylinder capability stated in the SDD rather than any quantitative endurance data.

assumptions.text: The failure-condition ids supplied this turn (SF-021-PL2, SF-022-M, SF-022-PL2) are authoritative for this AFHA even though the current FCIM rows carry different suffixes (SF-021-M3, SF-022-M, SF-022-PL3).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the ids should mirror the FCIM suffixes, the srcCondId trace links on these rows would need re-pointing to the correct FCIM conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: srcCondId on all five rows
assumptions.rationale: The instruction fixes the exact ids to cover, but the FCIM in project state does not enumerate all of them identically; a mapping decision is forced.

assumptions.text: Loss-of-oxygen conditions affect only the flight crew because the aircraft carries no passengers and the hold is unoccupied in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupant is carried in the hold in flight, both rows would gain a passenger-effect entry and SF-022-TL severity could rise.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL effPax, SF-022-PL3 effPax, SF-022-TL severity

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant-effect column needs to know who is exposed; the SDD states crew-only carriage, so passenger effects are not applicable.

assumptions.text: A rapid or gross depressurisation is credible at the FL260 low-differential operating concept such that crew oxygen is safety-relevant during descent/diversion.
assumptions.ifWrong: If emergency descent alone preserves safe flight at FL260 without crew oxygen, SF-022-TL could drop below Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL severity (Hazardous / HAZ-2)

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.rationale: SF-022-TL severity depends on the exposure the missing oxygen protects against; the SDD names loss-of-pressurisation as the design driver but does not quantify depressurisation severity at this altitude.

assumptions.text: Continuous flight-deck cylinder-pressure indication means a loss of stored quantity is normally detected, so the 'undetected' case requires a separate indication-defeating failure not described in the SDD.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a credible indication-defeating failure exists, SF-022-PL3 gains a statable aircraft effect and a non-empty severity could be derived.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-PL3 effAc (blank), SF-022-PL3 severity (blank)

citations.quote: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item.

assumptions.rationale: SF-022-PL3 is defined as UNDETECTED, but the SDD asserts continuous indication; without the mechanism that defeats it the in-flight aircraft effect cannot be grounded.

assumptions.text: Ground reverse thrust is a landing-rollout deceleration contributor on the semi-prepared strip, so SF-002 failure conditions are assessed in the landing/rollout phase.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust is not credited in the landing distance, SF-002-PL and SF-002-TL effects reduce toward Minor/No Safety Effect; if it is credited on the short strip, they may reach Major or worse.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-M2, SF-002-M3, SF-002-PL, SF-002-TL effect statements and (abstained) severities

citations.quote: Reverse deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states reverse deployment is inhibited in flight by WOW and radio-altimeter agreement, forcing the phase to ground rollout, but does not state whether reverse thrust is credited in the certified landing distance.

assumptions.text: The ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout is the basis for judging deceleration degradation, not a per-contributor allocation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust carries a defined share of the deceleration budget, SF-002-PL/TL severities would be classifiable directly from the margin consumed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-PL, SF-002-TL severityRationale (abstention)

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the two distances and calls the margin the basis for assessing braking degradation but does not allocate the margin between wheel braking and reverse thrust.

assumptions.text: Erroneous roll response can occur at low altitude / in a critical phase where recovery time and altitude are insufficient.
assumptions.ifWrong: If erroneous roll response is bounded to benign phases or limited magnitude, the SF-003-M severity would drop below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M severity (Catastrophic, CAT-1)
assumptions.rationale: The FHA rule requires classifying per flight phase and taking the worst; the function definition ('Control roll') does not itself bound the phase, so the worst-credible phase is assumed.

assumptions.text: SF-002-M2, SF-002-M3, SF-002-PL and SF-002-TL roll up under subId SF-002 rather than under split malfunction subIds.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-002 malfunctions are split into their own subIds, the subId field on these rows must change to match the model's convention.
assumptions.usedFor: subId field on all four SF-002 rows
assumptions.rationale: The model shows SF-008 malfunctions split into distinct subIds (SF-008-M, SF-008-M3, SF-008-M4) but the SF-002 malfunction conditions are not yet present as rows, so their subId mapping is inferred.

assumptions.text: An uncommanded roll (SF-003-M2) and a slow unaware roll divergence (SF-003-M3) can progress to an unrecoverable bank / loss of control if uncorrected.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an architectural stop or protection bounds the achievable uncommanded bank, SF-003-M2 and SF-003-M3 severities drop below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M2, SF-003-M3 severity (Catastrophic)

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the roll surfaces and their supplies but states no recovery-time or recoverable-attitude limits, so the progression to loss of control is inferred from function behaviour, not documented.

assumptions.text: 'Outside manoeuvre limits' (SF-003-PL2) means roll control is retained but authority is insufficient to meet the full required manoeuvre envelope, whereas 'within manoeuvre limits' (SF-003-PL) means required manoeuvres remain achievable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the boundary is defined differently, SF-003-PL2 (Hazardous) and SF-003-PL (Major) severities may shift.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-PL severity (Major), SF-003-PL2 severity (Hazardous)

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.rationale: The condition titles distinguish within/outside manoeuvre limits but the SDD does not define the manoeuvre-limit boundary for roll, so the capability shortfall each implies is interpreted.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so there are no passengers and occupant effects are limited to flight crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried, the occupant-effect column and possibly severities would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all five SF-003 rows

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Occupant effects are needed for each row; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight.

assumptions.text: The split-rudder arrangement guarantees residual yaw authority covering the outboard-engine-out sizing case when high-lift is within manoeuvre limits.
assumptions.ifWrong: If residual authority does not cover the sizing case, SF-005-PL is more severe than Minor and the MIN-1 anchor no longer applies.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-PL severity (Minor / MIN-1)

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts a single supply loss must leave sufficient authority but does not quantify the residual margin for a within-limits degradation, forcing a judgement to propose Minor.

assumptions.text: On the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, total loss of wheel braking produces an overrun beyond the prepared surface with loss of the airplane.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverser plus aerodynamic braking stops the aircraft within available distance, SF-008-TL drops from Catastrophic to Hazardous or Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL severity (Catastrophic), SF-008-M2 severity (Hazardous)

citations.quote: The landing distance requirement is 1,800 m (6,000 ft) on such a surface. Predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the requirement and predicted rollout but does not quantify residual deceleration from reversers/aero alone or the overrun terrain, forcing a worst-case operational assumption.

assumptions.text: A false 'down-and-locked' indication that conceals a genuinely unlocked unit can lead to gear collapse and loss of ground support at that unit.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the dual independent sensing makes a false-locked indication non-credible without an actual collapse, SF-007-M may downgrade from Hazardous to Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007-M severity (Hazardous), SF-007-PL2 severity (Major)

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual independent downlock sensing per unit but does not state the failure mode by which both the indication and the actual downlock could be defeated together, forcing a worst-case architecture assumption.

assumptions.text: Asymmetric braking on a limited-width semi-prepared strip during a high-energy stop threatens directional control margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: If strip width and steering authority absorb asymmetric braking within margin, SF-008-M2 downgrades from Hazardous to Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-M2 severity (Hazardous)

citations.quote: Anti-skid operates per wheel pair.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the strip length and flotation basis but not the strip width or the directional-control margin during braking, forcing an operational assumption to classify the asymmetric case.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight so no passenger effects apply to any of these conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were ever carried in the hold, occupant effects would need re-assessment for the ground-support and braking conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all five rows

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Effect-on-passengers must be stated; the SDD confirms flight-crew-only operation, so passenger effect is grounded rather than assumed benign.

assumptions.text: SF-013 is a monitoring/annunciation function whose failure is latent to the crew, so its severity is driven by the worst undetected restraint condition it fails to reveal rather than by any loss of restraint capability itself.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the loop also contributes to restraint control or load-sharing, the M/PL/TL effects and any eventual severity would be more severe and would need reframing as a restraint-capability loss.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-013-M2, SF-013-M3, SF-013-PL, SF-013-PL2, SF-013-TL effect statements

citations.quote: A tension monitoring loop instruments every strap continuously. Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes SF-013 as a tension monitoring loop that annunciates tension loss; it provides no restraint force itself, so its failure-condition effects must be framed as loss of detection.

assumptions.text: The crew has indication only in flight and cannot adjust restraint, so no crew mitigating action follows a restraint-tension event once monitoring is lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a crew procedure (e.g. descent, speed/manoeuvre restriction) meaningfully mitigates a developing restraint loss, the aware-case effects and severity of a monitoring failure would be reduced.
assumptions.usedFor: effCrew for all five SF-013 rows

citations.quote: In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.

assumptions.rationale: Needed to state the crew and aircraft effects; the SDD gives crew interaction but not a mitigation procedure for restraint loss.

assumptions.text: The aircraft-level consequence of an undetected restraint-tension loss (magnitude of blade shift, CG excursion or structural threat) is not quantified in the provided material.
assumptions.ifWrong: If this consequence is in fact bounded (benign) or hazardous, the severity fields left empty on all five rows could be committed to a class.
assumptions.usedFor: empty severity on SF-013-M2, SF-013-M3, SF-013-PL, SF-013-PL2, SF-013-TL

citations.quote: Longitudinal restraint is by two tension straps per saddle, tensioned by electric winches and locked mechanically.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the restraint architecture and annunciation thresholds but gives no relationship between restraint loss and aircraft controllability/structural limits, which is the datum needed to classify a monitoring failure.

assumptions.text: The flight deck is crewed by a nominal complement of two (up to four) and the hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effects for all five conditions are limited to flight crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold were occupied or complement differed, effPax and possibly the severity of SF-015-TL and the SF-016 conditions would change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015-TL, SF-016-M, SF-016-M2, SF-016-PL, SF-016-PL2 (effPax fields)

citations.quote: The aircraft carries flight crew only — a nominal complement of two, with provision for four.

assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant-effect column requires knowing who is aboard; the SDD states the crew complement and unoccupied hold, which I relied on to set effPax to 'no occupant effect'.

assumptions.text: Pressurisation control is a distinct function (SF-014) and remains available under SF-015-TL, so complete loss of ECS conditioning/distribution does not itself cause a cabin-altitude excursion.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-015-TL also removes pressurisation control, the aircraft effect and severity for SF-015-TL would escalate toward the SF-014 pressurisation-loss conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015-TL (effAc, severityRationale)

citations.quote: Pressurisation control is by two digital controllers driving two outflow valves, either valve being sufficient.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD separates pressurisation control from conditioning/distribution; I scoped SF-015-TL to conditioning/distribution only to avoid double-counting the SF-014 pressurisation effect.

assumptions.text: SF-016-PL2 'reduced protection capacity when heating demand shared' refers to the IPS bleed demand that reduces ECS pack capacity via the shared cross-bleed manifold, not an internal IPS-only sharing.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-016-PL2 means an intra-IPS electrical-zone sharing instead, the effAc and severityRationale would need to be restated against the electrical heating zones rather than the bleed/pack interaction.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016-PL2 (effAc, severityRationale)

citations.quote: a bleed demand to the environmental system that reduces pack capacity when in use

assumptions.rationale: The condition text is terse; the only shared-heating-demand mechanism in the SDD is the cross-bleed manifold shared between IPS bleed protection and the ECS packs, which I used to state the aircraft effect.

assumptions.text: The aircraft is operated in the icing envelope of its certification basis, so ice-protection loss and detection failures have an in-service exposure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the aircraft were never certified/dispatched into icing, SF-016-TL and the SF-017 detection failures would have no safety effect and their severity would collapse toward No Safety Effect.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016-TL, SF-017-M, SF-017-M2, SF-017-TL effect statements

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the IPS exists for flight in the icing envelope but the FHA rows need an assumed exposure to icing to have any aircraft effect at all.

assumptions.text: Heated probes and static ports feed the primary air-data (ADIRU) chain, so loss of probe heating in icing can corrupt airspeed/angle-of-attack information.
assumptions.ifWrong: If probe heating does not gate the primary air-data used for flight, SF-017-TL and SF-017-M2 effects overstate the air-data threat and their eventual severity could be lower.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-TL and SF-017-M2 effect on aircraft

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists heated probes/static ports and separately three ADIRUs but does not explicitly wire the heated probes to the air-data sources; the air-data consequence of probe-heat loss is inferred.

assumptions.text: With one ice detector lost the second, opposite-side detector continues to provide icing detection independently.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common cause defeats both detectors together, SF-017-PL2 is not the bounding loss and the total-loss SF-017-TL dominates instead, changing the Minor classification.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-PL2 (Minor / MIN-1)

citations.quote: Two ice detectors of the same type are installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two detectors on opposite sides but calls out that they are identical in type (a common-cause candidate); the single-channel-loss row assumes the surviving detector is functionally independent for this condition.

assumptions.text: The integrated standby instrument gives the crew a usable independent flying reference after loss of the primary displays, making SF-018-PL2 a reduction rather than a total loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If standby-only flight is not sufficient in IFR at low flight levels, SF-018-PL2 approaches loss of information presentation and its severity rises toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-PL2 effects and empty severity

citations.quote: Standby attitude, airspeed and altitude are provided by an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus.

assumptions.rationale: The function definition does not state the residual flying capability on standby-only; the SDD asserts the standby instrument's independence but not its sufficiency for IFR flight.

assumptions.text: Misleading primary flight/navigation information can be flown into an unsafe aircraft state before the crew detects the discrepancy against the standby instrument.
assumptions.ifWrong: If crew cross-check reliably catches the discrepancy in time, SF-018-M2 could reduce below Catastrophic toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M2 severity (CAT-1)

citations.quote: hosts the alerting that tells the crew what has failed and what to do about it

assumptions.rationale: The provided material gives redundancy topology but no crew detection-time or cross-check reliability, which is what determines whether misleading data is recoverable.

assumptions.text: The masked case (undetected real fire) dominates SF-020-M and occurs in a fire zone where an undetected fire threatens the airplane.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the condition is scoped to the spurious case only, the proposed CAT-1 is wrong and severity drops materially.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-M severity (CAT-1) and the split recommendation

citations.quote: Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing  High energy, flammable fluid,  fire zone

assumptions.rationale: SF-020-M as listed merges spurious and masked behaviours with opposite consequences; the driving case must be assumed to set a single severity.

assumptions.text: After one oxygen cylinder vents overboard, the remaining cylinder still meets the required crew diversion duration (at reduced reserve).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the surviving cylinder cannot meet the required duration, SF-022-M is a genuine loss of adequate reserve and rises toward Major/Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-M effects and empty severity

citations.quote: either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states either cylinder can supply 'at reduced reserve' but does not quantify whether that reserve satisfies the diversion sizing; severity depends on that margin.

assumptions.text: The flight crew are the only occupants requiring oxygen and SF-022-TL is assessed coincident with the depressurisation/smoke/fume event it exists to cover.
assumptions.ifWrong: If assessed independent of a coincident event demand, the immediate aircraft effect is lower and severity is not Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL severity (CAT-1)

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.rationale: The condition's severity depends on the event it accompanies; the function definition ties crew oxygen to loss-of-pressurisation, smoke and fume events.

assumptions.text: Crew act on the misleading primary flight/navigation information before cross-checking the independent standby instrument.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a discrepancy is always detected and acted on before an unsafe state is commanded, SF-018-M2 could reduce below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M2 severity Catastrophic

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares nothing with the primaries but does not establish that a discrepancy is detected in time; the effect (and thus Catastrophic vs lower) depends on whether detection is assured.

assumptions.text: A masked (undetected) engine or APU fire progresses to a hazard capable of causing loss of the aircraft absent crew extinguishing action.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an undetected nacelle fire is reliably contained by design (e.g. burn-through protection) with adequate secondary cueing, SF-020-M masked case could reduce below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-M severity Catastrophic

citations.quote: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles

assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms crew-initiated extinguishing via fire handles but provides no data on how far an undetected fire progresses before secondary indication; the severity leans on fire progression outrunning response.

assumptions.text: Total loss of crew oxygen occurs coincident with a decompression, smoke or fume event requiring it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the loss is always detected and dispatch/diversion precludes exposure to a demanding event, SF-022-TL could reduce below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL severity Catastrophic

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.rationale: The SDD sizes the system for those events but the FHA effect (crew incapacitation) only materialises when the loss and the demanding event co-occur; classification is driven by that worst-case coincidence.

assumptions.text: The single spanwise cross-feed gallery is a common fuel path whose failure can simultaneously affect fuel supply to multiple engines.
assumptions.ifWrong: If per-engine collector feeds are fully independent of the gallery for all engines, the gallery contributor drops out and the four engine branches become strictly independent, tightening the AND with no shared event.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-TL: 'Cross-feed gallery / isolation path fails to supply engine N' basic events under each engine's fuel OR-gate

citations.quote: Cross-feed is by a single gallery running spanwise through the wing box

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the gallery is the only path between sides but does not decompose per-engine isolation-valve independence, forcing a common-cause representation.

assumptions.text: Each engine's thrust generation is independent of the others (separate zones, separate services, four FADEC power sources), so complete loss requires all four to fail.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common cause (e.g. shared bus, shared fuel event) can fail multiple engines together, the top event acquires a lower-order cut set and the AND structure understates risk.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-TL: top-level AND across the four engine branches

citations.quote: no single bus loss can affect more than one engine

assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts separation but independence is a claim to be tested, not established fact; the AND across engines leans on it.

assumptions.text: The three dissimilar FCCs vote/monitor such that a single erroneous computation is contained unless the voting defence is also defeated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the voting does not contain a single-channel erroneous command, the AND collapses toward an order-1 cut set, which is unacceptable for a Catastrophic top event and would require re-architecting the branch.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M: 'Erroneous roll command generated by flight control computers reaches surfaces' AND-gate

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes three dissimilar computers voting but does not detail the vote/monitor coverage, forcing the AND (erroneous output AND containment failure).

assumptions.text: Roll surfaces comprise ailerons (on HYD B and C) and multi-function spoilers, each with its own actuator control electronics.
assumptions.ifWrong: If spoilers do not contribute to commanded roll or ACE topology differs, the roll-surface OR branch changes membership.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M: 'Erroneous actuator-control-electronics command to a roll surface' OR-gate

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names ailerons and spoilers for roll and dual actuation per surface but does not enumerate the actuator-control-electronics per surface, so the ACE contributors are modelled at the surface level the document resolves.

assumptions.text: An erroneous roll command reaching the aileron actuators requires both a faulted FCC and a failure of the command-voting/comparator to reject it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the voting monitor makes an erroneous command require coincident failures, the FCC command branch of SF-003-M2 and the low-rate command source of SF-003-M3 become AND gates rather than single OR inputs, removing an order-1 cut set.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M2 command branch ('Erroneous roll command generated by flight control computers'); SF-003-M3 slow-source 'Low-rate erroneous roll command from flight control computer'

citations.quote: Primary control is fly-by-wire with three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar FCCs vote on command but does not document the comparator/monitor logic or its coverage, so I could not decide whether the command branch is an OR (single) or an AND (coincident) contributor.

assumptions.text: There is no dedicated roll-rate/attitude divergence monitor beyond the primary display presentation and the consolidated crew alerting.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated roll-divergence monitor exists, the SF-003-M3 detection branch gains that contributor and its coverage may change whether the top event remains a plausible two-order AND.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M3 detection branch 'Roll divergence not detected / annunciated to crew'

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes display presentation and a consolidated alert list but does not name a specific slow-roll-divergence monitor or its threshold, so the detection branch of SF-003-M3 was built from the AVI paths only.

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path does not drive roll surfaces and therefore contributes no independent uncommanded-roll source.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any mechanical path can move a roll surface, an additional basic-event source would need adding under both uncommanded-roll trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Both SF-003-M2 and SF-003-M3 source branches

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD limits mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment; nothing indicates a roll reversion path, so no reversion contributor was placed in either roll tree.

assumptions.text: The A/B shared wing-root run is not a common-cause contributor to the ailerons, which are supplied by HYD B and HYD C.
assumptions.ifWrong: If HYD B distribution to the ailerons shares the A/B wing-root run and can be lost with system A events, an aileron-supply CCF basic event must be added under SF-003-TL, weakening the AND independence.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL tree, aileron HYD B/C branches

citations.quote: the ailerons from B and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the A/B wing-root commonality but the ailerons draw on B and C, not A and B together; no aileron-specific CCF is stated.

assumptions.text: Multi-function spoilers provide sufficient standalone roll authority such that complete loss requires losing both ailerons AND spoilers.
assumptions.ifWrong: If spoilers cannot sustain roll control alone, the top AND collapses toward an OR and the aileron branch alone may be an order-1 cut set for a Catastrophic condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL top-level AND gate

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists ailerons and spoilers as roll effectors but does not state the residual roll authority of spoilers alone.

assumptions.text: An erroneous (wrong-sense/magnitude) pitch output implies the 3-computer dissimilar vote is defeated by a common input or common-mode, rather than a single computer disagreeing.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single computer can drive an erroneous surface command without being outvoted, the FBW erroneous-command branch simplifies to single-computer basic events.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M erroneous-command branch

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes 3 dissimilar computers voting on command; a single erroneous computer would normally be outvoted, so an erroneous system output needs a common-mode or shared-input path.

assumptions.text: Elevators are supplied from HYD A and HYD C and the stabiliser is the third pitch effector, so erroneous surface response has three distinct paths.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the stabiliser or an elevator draws on a different supply, the HYD-path labelling under the erroneous-surface branch must be corrected.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M erroneous-surface-response branch

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states elevators from A and C and pitch by an all-moving stabiliser with elevators.

assumptions.text: An erroneous pitch command reaching the surface requires all three dissimilar flight control computers to output the erroneous command (modelled AND).
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single erroneous FCC output can drive the surface, the AND becomes an OR and the branch becomes an order-1 cut set, unacceptable for a Catastrophic condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M2 gate 'Erroneous pitch command survives the three-computer vote'; SF-004-M3 gate 'Slow erroneous pitch command survives three-computer vote'

citations.quote: Primary control is fly-by-wire with three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three computers vote on command but does not define the voting threshold or fault-containment for a corrupted command, forcing a conservative AND representation of the vote.

assumptions.text: The slow uncommanded pitch divergence is annunciated only through the AVI alerting system (two channels) and the pitch-attitude display, with no dedicated pitch-monitor documented.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated pitch-rate/divergence monitor exists, the detection-failure branch gains an additional independent input and the AND depth changes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M3 gate 'Failure to annunciate / display the pitch divergence to crew'

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD documents crew alerting and displays but does not describe any dedicated slow-divergence pitch monitor, so the detection branch is built solely from the alerting and display paths that exist.

assumptions.text: Uncommanded stabiliser-trim runaway and elevator actuator hardover are within the scope of the aircraft-level pitch-function tree rather than a lower system tree.
assumptions.ifWrong: If these belong to an FCS SFHA tree, they are removed from the AFHA tree and replaced by a transfer to the system tree.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M2 basic events 'Uncommanded stabiliser-trim runaway' and 'Elevator actuator hardover / uncommanded deflection'; SF-004-M3 slow-onset OR branch

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The provided FHA is aircraft-level and no SFHA/system rows exist yet; the SDD names these as pitch-surface contributors so they are carried at this level pending the system decomposition.

assumptions.text: The three FCC command paths to the elevator actuators are independent such that their loss must be combined under an AND gate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a shared resource defeats the three paths, the AND collapses toward an order-1 cut set and SF-004-TL structure fails the Catastrophic no-single-point rule.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL gate 'Loss of FCS command path to elevator actuators'

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar computers on different electrical sources but does not enumerate the elevator command-path failure logic at basic-event level.

assumptions.text: Elevator power is via HYD A and HYD C only, so loss of powered elevator control requires loss of both A and C.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a third supply or cross-connection exists the powered-elevator branch structure changes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL powered elevator AND gate

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns elevators to A and C but the tree needs this to set the AND logic.

assumptions.text: The stabiliser-trim mechanical reversion is a genuinely separate pitch means from powered elevators, so total pitch loss requires losing both.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion shares a resource with the elevators the top AND weakens toward a single point.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL top AND gate

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim

assumptions.rationale: SDD names a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim; the detailed independence from HYD/EPS is not fully described.

assumptions.text: A slow yaw divergence 'below detection threshold' requires both an uncommanded deflection source and independent failure/absence of the detection & alerting means.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated yaw-rate monitor exists and always annunciates, the 'crew unaware' branch and thus the whole FC structure changes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-M3 detection AND gate

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.rationale: The FC is defined by non-detection; the SDD does not specify the yaw-asymmetry monitor, so the detection branch is modelled from the alerting/display architecture generically.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of yaw authority requires loss of the upper segment path AND the lower segment path AND the mechanical reversion to the lower segment.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the segments are not fully independent (e.g. shared electronics), the top AND would collapse toward an OR and a single-point failure could appear, violating the Catastrophic no-order-1 rule.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL top AND gate and its two segment OR branches plus the reversion basic event

citations.quote: yaw by a split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with its own actuation and its own hydraulic supply
A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states each segment has its own actuation and hydraulic supply and that a mechanical reversion path exists to the lower rudder segment only, but does not give piece-part failure modes.

assumptions.text: Rudder upper is supplied by HYD A and rudder lower by HYD B.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the segment/supply mapping differs, the OR-branch basic-event labels for hydraulic loss are misassigned, though the AND logic and cut-set order are unchanged.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL segment OR branches; SF-005-PL3 degraded-supply basic event

citations.quote: A → rudder upper, elevators; B → rudder lower, ailerons; C → elevators, ailerons

assumptions.rationale: The interface matrix maps A→rudder upper and B→rudder lower, but the segment-to-actuation mapping detail below that is not enumerated.

assumptions.text: No yaw-specific slow-divergence / below-threshold monitor is defined in the architecture, so the detection branch of SF-005-PL3 is left undeveloped.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a yaw-degradation monitor exists, the detection OR branch must be populated with its real failure modes, which changes whether the 'unaware' AND is credibly independent.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-PL3 'Failure to detect / annunciate' OR branch (blank diamonds)

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.rationale: The SDD documents general crew alerting and FCS jam/asymmetry discretes but no yaw slow-divergence detection threshold; abstention rule requires leaving that content blank rather than inventing it.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of ground support / flotation (SF-007-TL) is a structural-integrity condition substantiated by structural analysis and Particular Risk Analysis, not a functional-contributor fault tree.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a functional-loss mechanism (e.g. common uplock/downlock or free-fall extension fault causing all-gear collapse) exists, the SF-007-TL tree gains functional OR contributors and is no longer a bare structural AND.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007-TL tree structure

citations.quote: Saddles are pinned to hard points

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 describes the gear as pinned structure with no leg-level functional redundancy, and the SDD gives no functional contributor chain for a total loss of ground support; Appendix A flags leg/bogie count as preliminary.

assumptions.text: The nose gear unit and the left/right main bogie groups fail independently, so no single structural event takes all support simultaneously.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common structural or zonal event (e.g. fuselage-side fairing structural failure) can take multiple units, the AND collapses toward a single-point structural failure and the qualitative acceptability fails.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007-TL AND gate

citations.quote: six three-wheel main bogies, three per side, retracting into fuselage-side fairings

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 lists them as separate units retracting into fuselage-side fairings but does not state a shared structural failure path; independence is assumed to keep the Catastrophic top event free of an order-1 cut set.

assumptions.text: The three brake sources — normal (HYD B), alternate (HYD A) and accumulator emergency — are independent such that no single event defeats all three.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the shared gear-bay bundle routing constitutes a common cause across HYD A and B brake feeds, the two hydraulic legs are not independent and the AND no longer meets the Catastrophic objective — a CCF group and possibly restructuring are required.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL top AND gate; HYD A and HYD B pressure basic events

citations.quote: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent bundles

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.3 states dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve, but §5.6.5 records that brake lines A and B share the main gear bay in adjacent bundles, a recorded zonal/CCF item.

assumptions.text: The electrically-signalled brake control path is represented as a per-source signalling basic event because the SDD does not resolve whether the signalling path is common across the normal and alternate sources.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single brake control electronics path is common to both HYD A and HYD B braking, that path is an order-1 cut set (single-point failure) for a Catastrophic condition and must be pulled out as a shared contributor above the AND.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL brake control signalling basic events

citations.quote: electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated brake control

assumptions.rationale: §5.6.2 states 'electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated brake control' without defining the electrical channel architecture or whether one brake control unit serves both hydraulic supplies.

assumptions.text: The SF-010-M2 top event requires both the door being not-fully-closed and that condition going undetected, so detection failure is modelled as a required AND co-contributor.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a not-fully-closed door alone (with correct indication) is the intended hazard, the top gate collapses to the drive/latch OR branch and the detection AND branch is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M2 top AND gate and its 'Not-fully-closed condition not detected' branch

citations.quote: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is included in the take-off configuration check.

assumptions.rationale: The failure-condition text itself states 'undetected or accepted at dispatch', which the SDD does not otherwise decompose; I inferred detection failure is part of the top event.

assumptions.text: A false locked/secure confirmation requires BOTH the proximity harness and the mechanical indicator to erroneously read locked, because the two sensing paths are dissimilar and independent.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single sensing path drives the displayed confirmation without agreement logic, the sensing branch becomes an OR and each path is an order-1 cut set — unacceptable for Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-M sensing AND branch and the common-cause leaf

citations.quote: sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.2/§5.7.5 describe two dissimilar independently routed sensing circuits but do not quantify their independence, so I modelled them as an AND with an explicit common-cause leaf.

assumptions.text: The twelve rotary latches share a common torque shaft, making their collective failure to engage a single contributor rather than twelve independent events.
assumptions.ifWrong: If latches were independently driven, the latch contribution would be a high-order AND rather than a single basic event, weakening its cut-set significance.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M2 'Twelve rotary latches fail to engage on closure (common torque shaft)' basic event

citations.quote: Twelve rotary latches engage on closure, driven by a common torque shaft.

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.2 states the latches are driven by a common torque shaft; the SDD does not resolve individual latch failure modes.

assumptions.text: Both dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical indicator) must give a false 'locked' indication for erroneous confirmation to reach the crew, i.e. they are independent.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single sensing path alone can display 'locked/secure', SF-011-M3 has an order-1 cut set and the AND gate over the two sensing paths must become an OR — unacceptable for a Catastrophic condition without further mitigation.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-M3 lower AND gate over the two lock-sensing paths

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits: a proximity sensing harness reading pin position directly, and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual dissimilar independently routed sensing but does not state whether the take-off configuration monitor / display consolidates them such that either alone can drive a false secure indication.

assumptions.text: The pressure interlock is a single series element on the unlock command; the ECS residual-differential signal it consumes is a distinct contributor from the interlock logic itself.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the interlock is single-channel with no independent confirmation, SF-011-M2's inhibit branch is effectively order-1 and the AND with the residual-differential condition may not by itself meet the Catastrophic objective.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-M2 interlock-failure OR gate and its ECS-signal contributor

citations.quote: A pressure interlock in series with the unlock command.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes one interlock in series and one ECS-supplied pressure state, but does not decompose the interlock into redundant channels, so no deeper independent structure can be grounded.

assumptions.text: These ground/dispatch-originated door-lock faults are carried into flight as latent conditions relevant to a per-flight-hour Catastrophic objective.
assumptions.ifWrong: If unlock permission cannot be erroneously granted in flight and no latent path exists, the flight-phase framing and exposure basis of SF-011-M2 change and the tree scope narrows to ground operations.
assumptions.usedFor: Top-event framing of SF-011-M2 and SF-011-M3

citations.quote: The door is operated from a ground handling panel with the aircraft on jacks or on its gear, and cannot be operated in flight.

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.6 states the door cannot be operated in flight, so the failure conditions manifest as pre-flight latents; the SDD does not state the exposure/check regime.

assumptions.text: SF-011-TL is correctly modelled as an AND of (loss of locking) and (loss of both confirmation paths), i.e. both must be lost for the stated top event.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the intent is loss of locking OR loss of confirmation, the top gate becomes OR and the single-point structure and DAL allocation change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-TL top AND gate

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.rationale: The FC text names both 'locking and confirmation'; the SDD describes locking and sensing as separate provisions but does not state the FHA boolean relationship.

assumptions.text: The two dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical visual indicator) are independent, so both must fail to lose confirmation.
assumptions.ifWrong: A common cause defeating both paths becomes an order-1 cut set for the confirmation branch, unacceptable for Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-TL confirmation OR branch

citations.quote: a proximity sensing harness reading pin position directly, and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator

assumptions.rationale: SDD claims dissimilar and independently routed sensing but independence is a claim to be tested, not established fact.

assumptions.text: SF-012-M requires both mechanical-lock-without-rated-tension AND failure of monitoring to reveal it for the erroneous (undetected) condition to stand.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the FC is intended as the mechanical fault alone regardless of monitoring, the monitoring branch drops and the top gate becomes single-branch OR.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-M top AND gate

citations.quote: A tension monitoring loop instruments every strap continuously. Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM pairs this erroneous condition with an unaware case; the monitoring loop is the annunciation path but the FHA boolean is not stated in the SDD.

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented run whose coverage is a recognised single-point limitation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the loop is later dual/segmented, the monitoring branch gains structure and is no longer an order-1 contributor.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-M monitoring OR branch

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.rationale: SDD states the loop is single and its coverage is a recorded item; depth beyond the loop is not resolved by the architecture.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of longitudinal restraint requires loss of strap restraint at all stations OR a hold floor hard-point structural failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: The AND grouping and the number of independent strap-pair inputs change, altering whether an order-1 cut set exists in the strap branch.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-TL strap-restraint AND branch

citations.quote: Nine saddles with two straps each, with load paths sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours.

assumptions.rationale: §5.8.2/§5.8.3 describe nine saddles with two straps each and neighbour load-sharing, but do not state how many stations must fail for total loss; I modelled it as loss across the restraining set.

assumptions.text: The hold floor hard point is a single non-redundant load path and is therefore an order-1 (single-point) contributor to complete restraint loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If hard-point failure does not by itself constitute complete loss, this branch moves under the AND and the order-1 cut set disappears.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-TL hard-point basic event

citations.quote: There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points.

assumptions.rationale: §5.8.3 states no redundancy in the hard points; whether hard-point structural failure alone unrestrains the blade is a structural judgement I could not fully ground.

assumptions.text: The independent standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary display chain, so primary error plus standby failure is a valid AND (independent).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby shares a common element, the AND collapses toward an OR and erroneous primary information becomes a single-point path.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M primary-chain-AND-standby branch

citations.quote: a standby instrument sharing nothing with the primaries

assumptions.rationale: §5.11.3 asserts independence; the tree's AND logic for the detectable-error branch depends on it holding.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/nav information can arise from an undetected common-source corruption that defeats the three-way reference-unit voting and dual-network comparison.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no credible common-mode source exists, that OR branch is removed and the top event reduces to the AND-protected path only.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M common-source corruption OR branch
