praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread — main or nose gear tyre failure releasing tread and casing fragments at ground speed (20 tyres: 6 three-wheel main bogies + twin-wheel nose unit)
praData.desc: Tyre burst or tread separation in a main gear bay (710/720) or nose gear bay (730). Debris energy/trajectory model NOT grounded — SDD states tyre sizing derived from a tactical airlifter but gives no tyre dimensions, burst pressure or fragment mass, so the debris size/energy/trajectory is left for the analyst. In-zone, a main gear bay houses three bogies each, brake lines A and B in adjacent separately-clipped bundles, and steering/brake harnesses; the nose bay houses the steering actuator and tow disconnect. Cross-zone reach is via the brake hydraulic A/B routing (710,720,300) which co-locates HYD A and B brake lines in each bay — the recorded zonal item where systems A and B brake supply share the bay. Installation is at drawing/model stage; gear leg/bogie count is preliminary per SDD §1.2.
praData.csfl: Co-location of brake hydraulic lines A and B in each main gear bay is the credible common-cause: a single tyre-burst event in a bay could damage both the normal (HYD B) and alternate (HYD A) brake supply that the AFHA fault tree for complete loss of wheel braking treats as an AND of independent supplies (page-1788106623620-894, gates 161/164). That defeats the independence claim on which SF-008-TL rests. Accumulator-supported emergency braking (gate 167) is a separate hot-battery/accumulator path retained.
praData.mitigation:
Proposed requirements: • The main and nose gear bay installation shall demonstrate that a credible tyre-burst debris trajectory cannot simultaneously sever brake hydraulic lines A and B within a single gear bay (separation, shielding, or routing on opposite sides of the bay).
• The steering and brake electrical harnesses shall remain routed on opposite sides of each gear bay such that a single tyre-burst trajectory cannot take both.
aiFunctions: SF-007 Support aircraft on ground and provide flotation
aiRequirements: The main and nose gear bay installation shall demonstrate that a credible tyre-burst debris trajectory cannot simultaneously sever brake hydraulic lines A and B within a single gear bay (separation, shielding, or routing on opposite sides of the bay).
The steering and brake electrical harnesses shall remain routed on opposite sides of each gear bay such that a single tyre-burst trajectory cannot take both.

praData.threat: Bird strike — external impact on forward-facing structure, engine inlets, windshields and probes. Bird mass / speed impact envelope NOT grounded (deferred to type-design bird envelope; not stated in SDD).
praData.desc: Bird strike on the nose visor structure (110), flight deck windshields (130), and engine inlets/nacelles (610–640). Impact energy model NOT grounded — the bird mass and airspeed envelope is not stated in the SDD and is deferred to the type-design bird envelope, so the impact case is left for the analyst. In-zone: the nose visor (110) carries the visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator and sensing harness and is the pressure boundary and forward structural load path when closed; the flight deck (130) houses displays, standby instrument and crew oxygen masks; the nacelles (610–640) house engine, FADEC, generator, EDP and fire detection loops. Probes/static ports/ice detectors are on the forward fuselage (electrically heated, monitored individually per IPS). Cross-zone: a nacelle ingestion striking an engine reaches EPS (one 150 kVA generator per engine) and HYD (one EDP per engine, A←eng 1,2 / B←eng 3,4) via the accessory-gearbox drive. The FADEC channels take power from four different sources so no single bus loss affects more than one engine. Installation at drawing/model stage.
praData.systems: PRP, NZD, AVI, IPS, ECS (pressure boundary), EPS, HYD
praData.csfl: A bird ingested into one engine is a single-engine event; the design continues after loss of any one engine, and the outboard-engine-failure-at-V1 case sizes directional control (rudder split-segment A/B). The multi-engine common-cause concern is a flocking event striking more than one inlet — outboard and inboard engines on one side share no service outboard of the wing root, but simultaneous ingestion is retained as a survivability case. A windshield/probe strike defeating multiple air-data sources feeds the AFHA erroneous-flight-information trees (SF-018-M, page-1788106623724-270 / page-1788106623738-416), where common-source air-data corruption is already modelled; standby instrument shares no sensor with the primaries. A visor structural strike bears on the nose-door pressure-boundary and structural load-path (SF-010-M2, SF-011 family) — the door is a single load path treated as structure.
praData.mitigation:
Proposed requirements: • The engine inlet installation shall demonstrate continued safe flight and landing following bird ingestion consistent with §33.76 / §25.571(e)(1) across the type-design bird envelope, including a credible multiple-ingestion (flocking) case on one side.
• The forward fuselage air-data and probe installation shall demonstrate that a single bird-strike trajectory cannot simultaneously corrupt or disable enough air-data sources to produce undetected erroneous flight information, preserving the independent standby instrument.
• The nose visor structure and its lock/sensing installation shall demonstrate that a credible bird strike does not defeat both the pressure boundary and the dual dissimilar lock-sensing paths.
aiFunctions: SF-018 Present flight and navigation information
SF-017 Heat probes and detect icing
SF-011 Lock and confirm nose door closure
aiRequirements: The engine inlet installation shall demonstrate continued safe flight and landing following bird ingestion consistent with §33.76 / §25.571(e)(1) across the type-design bird envelope, including a credible multiple-ingestion (flocking) case on one side.

The forward fuselage air-data and probe installation shall demonstrate that a single bird-strike trajectory cannot simultaneously corrupt or disable enough air-data sources to produce undetected erroneous flight information, preserving the independent standby instrument.
The nose visor structure and its lock/sensing installation shall demonstrate that a credible bird strike does not defeat both the pressure boundary and the dual dissimilar lock-sensing paths.

praData.threat: HIRF — High-Intensity Radiated Fields (§25.1317, AC 20-158A) — external RF environment coupling into electrical/electronic systems
praData.desc: External radiated field coupling through apertures and onto the six EWS routes into the flight-critical avionics and flight-control electronics. Coupling targets: the three FCCs in the forward/mid/aft equipment bays, the three display processing units, the three ADIRUs, both dual-redundant data network channels, the dual alerting processing channels and the actuator control electronics. The standby instrument shares no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries but is on the DC essential bus, so a HIRF upset of DC-essential-fed avionics is the correlated-failure branch to examine.
praData.csfl: A single HIRF environment illuminates the whole airframe at once and can upset all three dissimilar FCCs, both network channels and both alerting channels together — the dissimilarity and dual-channel independence claims for FCS voting, AVI display and crew alerting are common-mode-defeated unless equipment-level HIRF qualification and bundle shielding are substantiated.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact (forward-facing structure and inlets) — §25.571(e)(2)
praData.desc: Hail impact on forward-facing surfaces: nose visor structure (110) which is both pressure boundary and forward structural load path when closed; flight-deck windshields and probes (130); engine inlet cowls of nacelles 1-4 (610-640); wing leading edges (510/520). Impact energy on the nose visor is of particular note — the visor is a single load path treated as structure with no structural redundancy (SDD 5.7.3). Ice detectors and heated probes/static ports/windshields are on the forward fuselage (130) in the hail footprint. Drawing/model stage: bundle build and clamping positions are preliminary, so co-location conclusions are provisional.
praData.systems: NZD (nose visor, zone 110), AVI (windshields/probes/ice detectors, zone 130), PRP (engine inlets, zones 610-640), FCS/IPS (wing leading edges, zones 510/520)
praData.csfl: Hail striking both forward-fuselage ice detectors (same type, opposite sides of forward fuselage, SDD 5.10.2/5.10.3 records commonality) is a candidate common cause defeating the two nominally independent detection channels; hail degrading multiple heated probes feeding the three air-data reference units is a candidate common source for erroneous/misleading flight & nav information (SF-018-M).
praData.mitigation:
Forward-facing structure and windshields substantiated to the hail/ice-impact envelope of §25.571(e)(2); nose visor structural substantiation (single load path — structural analysis + PRA per App L, not a functional-FHA item); engine inlet hail ingestion substantiated at engine level (existing certified 330 kN-class turbofan); probe/detector heating and monitoring per IPS. Outcome claimed: MINIMISED for structure/inlets; ice-detector common-type susceptibility to be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE pending IPS FHA and detector dissimilarity/masking argument.
Proposed requirements: • Nose visor structure (zone 110) shall withstand the hail-impact energy of the §25.571(e)(2) envelope without loss of pressure-boundary or structural-load-path integrity.
• Windshields and heated probes/ports (zone 130) shall retain function following hail impact to the certification envelope such that erroneous flight & navigation information (SF-018-M) is not produced.
• The two forward-fuselage ice detectors shall not both be defeated by a single hail encounter (defeats the recorded same-type commonality, SDD 5.10.3).
aiFunctions: SF-010 Open and close the nose cargo door
SF-011 Lock and confirm nose door closure
SF-018 Present flight and navigation information
SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice
SF-017 Heat probes and detect icing
aiRequirements: Nose visor structure (zone 110) shall withstand the hail-impact energy of the §25.571(e)(2) envelope without loss of pressure-boundary or structural-load-path integrity.

Windshields and heated probes/ports (zone 130) shall retain function following hail impact to the certification envelope such that erroneous flight & navigation information (SF-018-M) is not produced.
The two forward-fuselage ice detectors shall not both be defeated by a single hail encounter (defeats the recorded same-type commonality, SDD 5.10.3).

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding — §25.1419, AC 20-73A (type-design ice envelope)
praData.desc: Ice accretion on unprotected or under-protected surfaces and ice shed from wing leading edges (510/520) or fuselage into the four engine inlets (610-640). Wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls are bleed-anti-iced from the shared cross-bleed manifold; stabiliser leading edges (zone 800) are electrically heated in six independent zones; probes/ports/windshields and the two ice detectors (130) are electrically heated. Loss or asymmetry of ice protection, or shed-ice inlet ingestion, is the concern. Hold pressurisation differential and gear/bogie counts are preliminary and do not bear on this study.
praData.systems: IPS (wing/cowl bleed protection, stabiliser electrical zones, probe/detector heating), PRP (inlet ingestion of shed ice), AVI (probe heat feeding air-data reference units), ECS (cross-bleed manifold shared with IPS)
praData.csfl: The wing/cowl anti-ice and the ECS packs draw from the SAME cross-bleed manifold in zone 300 (SDD 5.9.2/5.10.2) — a manifold fault is a candidate common cause reducing both conditioning and bleed ice protection; the two same-type ice detectors are a recorded common-type source; iced-over probes feeding all three air-data reference units are a candidate common source for erroneous flight & nav (SF-018-M).
praData.mitigation:
Ice protection sized to the certification icing envelope; bleed protection available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold; six independently supplied stabiliser zones with lost-zone annunciation; individually monitored heated probes; engine inlet ice-shed tolerance substantiated at engine level. Outcome claimed: MINIMISED for accretion via IPS coverage; shed-ice inlet ingestion and detector common-type susceptibility to be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE pending IPS FHA build-out.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall maintain airframe, inlet and probe protection across the type-design icing envelope such that no single failure produces an unannunciated loss of protection.
• Ice shed from wing leading edges or forward fuselage shall not cause loss of forward thrust (SF-001-TL) or asymmetric thrust (SF-001-M) beyond the substantiated inlet ice-ingestion capability.
• Icing of heated probes/ports shall not produce erroneous or misleading flight and navigation information (SF-018-M) undetected by air-data comparison/voting.
aiFunctions: SF-016 Protect airframe and inlets from ice
SF-017 Heat probes and detect icing
SF-018 Present flight and navigation information
aiRequirements: The ice protection system shall maintain airframe, inlet and probe protection across the type-design icing envelope such that no single failure produces an unannunciated loss of protection.
Ice shed from wing leading edges or forward fuselage shall not cause loss of forward thrust (SF-001-TL) or asymmetric thrust (SF-001-M) beyond the substantiated inlet ice-ingestion capability.
Icing of heated probes/ports shall not produce erroneous or misleading flight and navigation information (SF-018-M) undetected by air-data comparison/voting.

praData.threat: Cabin/cargo fire — hold fire (blade payload zone), smoke detection fitted, no suppression
praData.desc: Fire or smouldering in the unoccupied low-differential hold (stations 1-9). Nine smoke detectors along the length annunciate; NO hold suppression is fitted (SDD §5.12.2), so an established hold fire cannot be extinguished in flight. Fire/heat in the hold can attack the restraint tension monitoring loop (single left-side run), the fuel gallery vent, the left-side LV electrical route, and the three flight control computers distributed one per hold-adjacent equipment bay (FCC1 fwd 120, FCC2 mid 300, FCC3 aft 400).
praData.systems: CRG, FPR, FCS, FUE, AVI, EPS
praData.csfl: A hold fire that reaches the mid equipment bay (zone 300) is a single physical cause able to attack FCC2 while heat/smoke propagation along the full-length routings threatens the FCC1 and FCC3 bays — a common-cause path across the nominally-independent three-computer FCS voting set. It can also defeat the single restraint tension monitoring loop and the single-run cross-feed gallery vent.
praData.mitigation: Nine-station smoke detection provides detection (minimise). Absence of suppression means the effect is not eliminated in the hold; survivability rests on the substantiation that a single blade + no palletised combustible load presents no sustained fuel for fire (SDD §5.12.2 — recorded assumption, NOT yet substantiated). Separation of FCC bays and dual/opposite-side routing of network channels are relied on but must be re-examined against fire propagation, not just electrical fault. Proposed: substantiate the no-combustible-load basis; assess whether detection-only meets §25.855; evaluate need for FCC bay fire barriers.

praData.threat: Cabin/cargo fire — forward equipment bay & flight deck fire
praData.desc: Fire or smoke in the pressurised, conditioned forward equipment bay (FCC1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks) or the occupied flight deck (displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks). A fire adjacent to the two HP oxygen cylinders is a specific concern (thermal discharge indicator fitted; cylinders sited outside any high-energy electrical zone per §5.13.5).
praData.csfl: A forward-bay fire attacks FCC1, forward avionics racks and the oxygen cylinders together. It threatens the primary display chain and, via smoke on the flight deck, the standby instrument and the crew's ability to don oxygen — the very means of surviving a smoke/fume event. The DC-essential-fed standby instrument shares zone 130 with the primary displays it is meant to back up.
praData.mitigation: Crew oxygen quick-donning masks with smoke goggles (§5.13.2) and portable extinguisher at the flight deck (§5.12.2) support survivability of a flight-deck fire (minimise). Cylinders sited outside high-energy electrical zones and clear of the HV feeder route reduce ignition/aggravation. Detection coverage of zones 120/130 is NOT described in the SDD and cannot be grounded — flag as a gap for the analyst. Proposed: confirm forward-bay/flight-deck smoke detection provisions; assess FCC1 fire separation from the oxygen cylinders.

praData.threat: Cabin/cargo fire — aft fuselage & APU compartment fire
praData.desc: Fire in the aft fuselage / empennage, a mixed zone containing the rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders and the APU compartment (a designated fire zone). The APU compartment has dedicated dual-loop detection and a single bottle discharged automatically when unattended (§5.12.2).
praData.csfl: An aft-fuselage fire can attack the rudder control runs to both upper and lower segments (routed on opposite sides of the aft fuselage per §5.3.5/§4) and the stabiliser heater feeders in the same zone. Opposite-side routing is a spatial-separation independence claim that a zone-filling fire could defeat, threatening yaw control authority.
praData.mitigation: APU compartment carries dual-loop detection and automatic ground discharge (§5.12.2). Rudder upper/lower runs and stabiliser feeders are routed on opposite sides for separation (§5.3.5/§5.10.5). Bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat detection cover adjacent runs. In-flight APU fire extinguishing provision is not described and cannot be grounded — flag for the analyst. Proposed: confirm in-flight APU fire suppression; verify aft-fuselage fire cannot bridge both rudder segment runs.
aiFunctions: Protect airframe and inlets from ice

praData.threat: Lightning strike (§25.581/§25.1316, AC 20-136B) — direct attachment and indirect (conducted/coupled transient) effects
praData.desc: Direct attachment to extremities (wing tips, nose visor, empennage, nacelles, probes) and indirect coupling of lightning transients onto the six EWS routes. Zone-1/2 attachment surfaces conduct to structure; indirect transients couple into the HV feeder route (610/620,530,300,200), the LV signal route, the two data network channels and the DC-essential-fed standby/FCC/AVI feeders. The two identified HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 (shielded, not physically separated) and the fuel gallery through the wing box are the installation features to examine as common transient/ignition paths.
praData.systems: AVI, FCS, EPS, EWS, FUE, IPS (probe/detector heaters), FPR (detection loops)
praData.csfl: A single strike can inject correlated transients into all three dissimilar FCCs, both data network channels, both bus power control units and all three ADIRUs simultaneously — defeating the dissimilarity/separation independence claimed for FCS command voting and for AVI display/alerting. Fuel-vapour ignition at wing-box/tank interfaces is the additional catastrophic path.

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — pressure boundary when closed, unpressurised when open (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Visor latches (12 rotary, common torque shaft), 8 lock pins, lock actuator, lock sensing harness
zsaData.interference: Lock sensing harness (110→120→130) routed opposite door actuation power; common torque shaft is a single back-drive path for all 12 latches (SDD §5.7.2). Maintenance error risk: mis-rigging latch/pin engagement or sense-harness swap giving erroneous lock-secure indication with pins not fully driven.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify dual dissimilar sensing (proximity harness + mechanical visual indicator) independence at both bulkhead penetrations; confirm torque-shaft common-cause is captured in CMA; pressure interlock (<0.1 psi) proven in series with unlock command.

zsaData.equip: FCC 1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks; LV signal route + data network ch1/ch2 + nose-door lock sensing harness transit
zsaData.interference: Oxygen cylinders co-located with avionics/electrical energy sources — inherent hazard (cylinder overpressure/leak) on neighbouring FCC 1 and racks regardless of functional criticality (App K.3.1). SDD §5.13.5 states cylinders are 'outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source' — VERIFY this against forward avionics racks in same zone; potential conflict.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm cylinder installation separation from avionics energy sources; thermal discharge routed overboard; verify FCC 1 (one of three dissimilar computers) bay separation from FCC 2/3 preserved.

zsaData.equip: Displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks; nose-door lock sensing harness terminates here
zsaData.interference: Standby instrument must share no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays (SDD §5.11.3) — verify routing independence at flight-deck bulkhead. Maintenance-error risk: cross-connection of standby feed onto primary display route defeating the independence claim.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify standby instrument DC-essential wiring independent of primary display feeders; confirm fire-handle wiring integrity; mechanical lock visual indicator visible from flight deck confirmed.

zsaData.desc: Forward hold stations 1–3 — low differential, unoccupied (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3, restraint straps, tension monitoring loop, smoke detectors; HV feeder + LV signal + data ch1/2 + HYD C run + restraint loop transit
zsaData.interference: Restraint tension monitoring loop is a SINGLE instrumented run, full hold length, left side, sharing the hold zone with the fuel-gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (SDD §5.8.5) — recorded co-location item. HV feeder transits this zone. Single-loop coverage means one damage event can blind restraint monitoring over its length.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm HV/loop/fuel-vent minimum separation per EWS §5.14.2; capture single-loop coverage as CMA/PRA item; hold smoke detection present, NO suppression (SDD §5.12.2 — recorded assumption to substantiate).

zsaData.desc: Mid hold stations 4–6 — low differential, unoccupied (SDD §3). Convergence zone for the majority of zone-spanning routings.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points; HYD A/B wing-root run, HYD C run, fuel gallery, brake lines A/B, bleed cross-bleed manifold, HV feeders L/R, LV signal, data ch1/2 all transit
zsaData.interference: HIGH-DENSITY co-location: this is the one zone where HYD A+B share a wing-root run, the single fuel cross-feed gallery passes, brake lines A/B cross, the cross-bleed manifold joins both sides, AND the two HV/LV crossing points sit (SDD §4, §5.5.5). A single zonal event here can defeat multiple nominally independent redundancies (HYD A/B, both HV feeders, both data channels if separation is compromised). FCC 2 also housed here.
zsaData.mitigation: This zone drives the CMA: every AND-gate independence claim touching HYD A/B, fuel gallery, HV feeders and data channels must be tested for a common zonal cause here (ARP4761A common-mode). Verify the two HV/LV crossing points use shielding + defined minimum distance; confirm FCC 2 bay separation.

zsaData.desc: Aft hold stations 7–9 — low differential, unoccupied (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3; HYD C run + LV signal + data ch1/2 + restraint loop transit
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 (third dissimilar computer) housed here; restraint loop and HYD C transit. Maintenance-error risk: aft bay work disturbing FCC 3 or HYD C routing. Restraint loop continues its single-run coverage into this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify FCC 3 bay independence from FCC 1/2; confirm HYD C separation from A/B maintained (routed opposite side per §4); restraint-loop single-coverage captured as item.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Fuel tanks (outboard/mid/inboard cells), cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Flammable fluid zone with hot bleed anti-ice ducting AND the outboard electrical route sharing the leading edge behind a shielded partition (SDD §5.10.5). Inherent hazard: fuel/ignition-source proximity. Anti-ice duct hot surface adjacent to fuel structure.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify shielded partition integrity along full run; confirm tank vent/surge lines routed outboard of electrical harnesses (§5.2.5); reconcile with Ice, Lightning, HIRF PRAs.

zsaData.desc: Right wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present (SDD §3, mirror of 510).
zsaData.equip: Fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route; single pressure refuel/defuel point in right wing root (§5.2.2)
zsaData.interference: As 510, plus the single pressure refuel/defuel point with independent overflow protection (§5.2.2) — refuelling maintenance-error / overfill risk in a flammable zone. Hot anti-ice duct adjacent to fuel; outboard electrical route shares leading edge behind shielded partition.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify overflow protection independence; confirm shielded partition; reconcile with Ice/Lightning/HIRF PRAs.

zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit; fuel gallery + bleed duct also transit
zsaData.interference: RECORDED RED-LINE ITEM: HYD systems A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (SDD §5.3.5, §5.4.5, §4). This defeats the nominal A/B independence for any single zonal event here (fire, penetration, hot bleed rupture) — directly bears on the Catastrophic pitch/roll/yaw complete-loss FCs which rely on A/B/C separation. Bleed duct hot-surface + HV feeder co-located.
zsaData.mitigation: Carry HYD A/B shared-run as an explicit common-cause contributor in the SF-004-TL / SF-005-TL / SF-003-TL fault trees (ARP4761A: reflect the single cause rather than trust logical redundancy); verify bleed-duct/HV/hydraulic minimum separation; dedicated CMA item.

zsaData.desc: Right wing root — pressure-boundary transit (SDD §3, mirror of 530).
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit; fuel gallery + bleed duct transit
zsaData.interference: As 530: HYD A/B shared wing-root run defeating A/B independence for a single zonal event; hot bleed duct and HV feeder co-located crossing the pressure boundary.
zsaData.mitigation: As 530 — reflect HYD A/B common cause in the affected control-axis fault trees; verify separation; CMA item.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 (left outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 1, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops (A/B, opposite sides), extinguisher plumbing; HV feeder L + bleed duct originate here
zsaData.interference: Fire zone with high-energy rotating machinery and flammable fluid — inherent-hazard source affecting neighbouring zones via debris and fire (App K.3.1). Outboard engine at 28 m moment arm. Dual detection loops routed opposite sides with AND logic degrading to single-loop.
zsaData.mitigation: Reconcile with Rotor Burst / Engine Burst PRAs (uncontained debris trajectory to wing, feeders, opposite nacelle); verify loop A/B separation; two-bottle cross-plumbing per engine pair confirmed.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 2 (left inboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone. Thrust reverser fitted (inboard).
zsaData.equip: Engine 2, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing, thrust reverser
zsaData.interference: As nacelle fire zone, plus thrust reverser (inboard engines only, §5.1.2) — inadvertent deployment inhibits by WoW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock. Rotor/engine burst inherent hazard to wing, fuel, feeders.
zsaData.mitigation: Reconcile with Rotor/Engine Burst PRAs; verify reverser inhibit logic independence; loop A/B separation; cross-plumbed bottle coverage.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 3 (right inboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone. Thrust reverser fitted (inboard).
zsaData.equip: Engine 3, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing, thrust reverser
zsaData.interference: As nacelle 2 (mirror). Engine 3 drives HYD B pump (§5.1.2) — nacelle 3 event affects HYD B source. Reverser + rotor/engine burst inherent hazards.
zsaData.mitigation: Reconcile with Rotor/Engine Burst PRAs; verify HYD B source redundancy (eng 3+4); reverser inhibit; loop separation.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 4 (right outboard) — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (SDD §3, mirror of 610).
zsaData.equip: Engine 4, FADEC, generator, EDP, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing; HV feeder R + bleed duct originate here
zsaData.interference: Outboard engine at 28 m moment arm (directional-control sizing case per §5.1.3). Engine 4 drives HYD B pump. Rotor/engine burst inherent hazard to wing, fuel, HV feeder R.
zsaData.mitigation: Reconcile with Rotor/Engine Burst PRAs; verify HYD B source (eng 3+4) and generator 4 independence; loop A/B separation; cross-plumbed bottle coverage.

cmaData.subject: G-001 independence — Engine 1 collector feed (both boost pumps AND gravity path)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Redundancy of engine-1 fuel feed: boost pump A, boost pump B, and gravity feed path treated as independent inputs to the AND gate.. The two engine-1 collector boost pumps and the gravity feed path fail independently, so simultaneous loss of engine-1 collector feed requires three independent failures.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (electrical): both boost pumps per collector are AC-driven (SDD §5.2.4 'AC power to the boost and transfer pumps') — a single AC source or bus loss can disable both pumps simultaneously, collapsing two of the three AND inputs. Common Design/Manufacturing: the two boost pumps are a matched parallel pair (SDD §5.2.2 'Two AC boost pumps per collector operate in parallel') with no stated dissimilarity — a common design or manufacturing-lot defect defeats both. Gravity path is not a co-equal third leg: it is available only below FL150 (SDD §5.2.2 'A gravity feed path exists below FL150'), so at cruise the AND gate effectively degrades toward the boost-pump pair alone. Common Environment: pumps and collector co-located; a wing-tank/collector-zone particular risk could strike both.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm the two boost pumps per collector draw from different AC buses so no single bus loss takes both; add a common-cause contributor (shared AC supply) as a repeated/CCF event under G-001 rather than leaving a bare AND; consider dissimilarity or staggered overhaul across the pump pair; carry the FL150 gravity-path limitation as an availability condition on the third AND input; reconcile against PRA/ZSA for the collector zone.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two boost pumps of the engine-1 collector shall be supplied from independent AC electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both.
• The gravity feed path shall be credited in the SF-001-TL fault tree only for flight phases below FL150.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Redundancy of engine-1 fuel feed: boost pump A, boost pump B, and gravity feed path treated as independent inputs to the AND gate.
aiRequirements: The two boost pumps of the engine-1 collector shall be supplied from independent AC electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both.
The gravity feed path shall be credited in the SF-001-TL fault tree only for flight phases below FL150.

cmaData.subject: G-010 Engine 4 collector feed — dual boost pumps + gravity path independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two parallel AC boost pumps per collector, each sufficient for full demand, backed by a gravity feed path below FL150.. Engine 4 loses collector feed only if both boost pump A and boost pump B fail AND the gravity feed path is unavailable (AND-gate independence).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (electrical): both boost pumps are AC-driven and draw on the same AC distribution serving the collector — loss of that AC supply fails both pump inputs simultaneously. Common Resources (fuel/sensor): both pumps draw from the single collector cell; cell contamination or blockage starves both. Operation/Architecture: the gravity path is available only below FL150, so at cruise the AND effectively reduces to the two boost pumps, which are NOT independent of shared AC. Development/Design: pumps are a common design/part type, exposing a common wear/quality mode.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm the two boost pumps take power from independent AC channels; specify collector-cell design/inspection against common contamination; retain and substantiate the gravity path as a genuinely dissimilar principle and bound its FL150 applicability against the failure condition's flight phase.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two Engine 4 collector boost pumps shall be supplied from independent electrical channels such that no single AC source loss disables both.
• The fuel system shall preclude a single collector-cell contamination or blockage from simultaneously starving both boost pumps.

aiRequirements: The two Engine 4 collector boost pumps shall be supplied from independent electrical channels such that no single AC source loss disables both.

cmaData.subject: G-013 Complete loss of forward thrust — four-engine independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Four independent podded turbofans, left/right services not commingled outboard of the wing root, dual-channel FADEC on four different power sources.. Complete loss of forward thrust requires loss of thrust from all four engines together (AND-gate independence across engines 1-4).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (fuel): all four engines are fed by the FUE resource; the cross-feed gallery is a SINGLE spanwise run through the wing box — the only path from one wing to the opposite engines (recorded PRA/zonal item) — so a gallery or common fuel-management fault, or contaminated/mis-managed fuel, is a common cause across all four. Development/Design: the engines are an existing common certified type with a common FADEC design and single generator/EDP part number — a common-mode design or software error in FADEC could affect multiple engines. Common Resources (bleed/electrical): shared cross-bleed manifold and EPS are common to all engines' starting/control. Installation: left and right pairs are zonally separated (zones 610/620 vs 630/640), which supports independence against localised events but not against the fuel and design commonalities.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the cross-feed gallery, fuel contamination, and common FADEC design as explicit common-cause contributors on the four-engine AND rather than leaving a falsely optimistic AND; substantiate fuel cleanliness/management independence and FADEC dissimilarity/software commonality; carry the single gallery into PRA and ZSA per its recorded status.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Common-cause contributors (single cross-feed gallery, common fuel supply/management, common FADEC design) shall be represented explicitly on the four-engine loss-of-thrust fault tree.
• The propulsion architecture shall preclude a single fuel-quality or fuel-management fault from simultaneously affecting all four engines.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Four independent podded turbofans, left/right services not commingled outboard of the wing root, dual-channel FADEC on four different power sources.
aiRequirements: Common-cause contributors (single cross-feed gallery, common fuel supply/management, common FADEC design) shall be represented explicitly on the four-engine loss-of-thrust fault tree.
The propulsion architecture shall preclude a single fuel-quality or fuel-management fault from simultaneously affecting all four engines.

cmaData.subject: G-014 Erroneous roll command — FCC dissimilar-voting independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command, each supplied from a different electrical source, hosting software from two teams under a dissimilarity argument, installed in three separate bays.. An erroneous roll command is generated only if a flight control computer produces an erroneous roll command AND the dissimilar voting / cross-monitor fails to catch it (AND-gate independence).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (data/sensor): all three FCCs consume common air-data and inertial inputs; a common-mode corruption of that shared source data can drive a consistent erroneous roll command that survives voting (the voter sees agreement, not truth). Development/Design (specification): dissimilar software mitigates independent coding faults but a common REQUIREMENT/specification error in the voting/comparator or control law is shared across all channels and defeats the dissimilarity argument. Common Resources (electrical): mitigated — three different electrical sources. Installation: mitigated — three separate bays (forward/mid/aft equipment bays, zones 120/300/400).
cmaData.mitigation:
Require input-data comparison/validation upstream of the voter so common-source data errors are rejected, not voted-through; specify and independently verify the voting/comparator and control-law specification against common requirement error; confirm the two-team dissimilarity covers the voting logic itself, not only the command computation.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The flight control system shall detect and reject erroneous common-source air-data/inertial inputs upstream of the roll command voter so that a common-mode input error does not survive voting.
• The roll command voting/comparator specification shall be independently verified against common requirement-level error that would defeat the dissimilarity argument.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command, each supplied from a different electrical source, hosting software from two teams under a dissimilarity argument, installed in three separate bays.
aiRequirements: The flight control system shall detect and reject erroneous common-source air-data/inertial inputs upstream of the roll command voter so that a common-mode input error does not survive voting.
The roll command voting/comparator specification shall be independently verified against common requirement-level error that would defeat the dissimilarity argument.

cmaData.subject: G-023 independence — slow uncommanded roll source vs. roll-divergence detection/annunciation (page 'Slow uncommanded roll divergence below detection threshold')
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence between the roll-command/actuation drift path and the detection & crew-alerting path.. The slow-rate uncommanded roll source and the failure-to-detect/annunciate branch are independent, so both must fail for the below-threshold divergence to occur.
cmaData.findings: Development phase (supports PSSA). The detection branch depends on roll attitude/rate presentation and crew alerting, both hosted in the AVI chain; the alerting system runs on two independent processing channels but the standby/essential presentation and alerting both draw on the DC essential bus (SDD §5.5.2 lists FCS computers, standby instruments and indication on the DC essential bus). A DC-essential degradation, or a common ADIRU/air-data source error feeding both the FCC low-rate command AND the displayed attitude, couples the drift source to the detector. Physical: both the FCC command path and the display/alerting converge in the mid equipment bay / zone 300. Common resource (DC essential, ADIRU data), Development/Design (common air-data source), Installation-Design (zone 300 convergence).
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the roll-divergence monitor to use a source dissimilar/independent from the command that could produce the slow drift; require the detection & alerting path to survive loss of the source feeding the drift; substantiate the two alerting channels do not share the single failure that could mask a below-threshold divergence; keep drift-source and monitor on independent power segregation.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The roll-divergence detection shall use an attitude/rate source independent of the command source capable of producing a below-threshold slow roll drift.
• The crew-alerting path for roll divergence shall remain available under loss of any single electrical supply that also affects the roll-command path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence between the roll-command/actuation drift path and the detection & crew-alerting path.
aiRequirements: The roll-divergence detection shall use an attitude/rate source independent of the command source capable of producing a below-threshold slow roll drift.
The crew-alerting path for roll divergence shall remain available under loss of any single electrical supply that also affects the roll-command path.

cmaData.subject: G-026 independence — loss of aileron roll effectors (ailerons on HYD B and HYD C)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence between the HYD B aileron supply and the HYD C aileron supply.. Loss of the aileron effectors requires simultaneous loss of the HYD B supply AND the HYD C supply to the aileron actuators (plus actuation/surface integrity), which are claimed independent.
cmaData.findings: Development phase (supports PSSA). Hydraulic sourcing is genuinely independent: system B is engine-driven (engines 3,4) and system C is electric-motor-pump with a RAT backstop (SDD §5.4.2), and C is 'Routed separately from A and B along the opposite side' (SDD §4, Hydraulic system C run). Note A and B share a wing-root run (SDD §5.4.5) but THIS gate pairs B with C, so that shared run is not the coupling. Residual common causes: (1) co-location of both aileron actuators and the aileron surfaces themselves within the wing structure — a single zonal/particular-risk event (zone 530/540 wing root or a wing-box event) or the 'Aileron actuation/surface mechanical' basic event common to both channels; (2) both C electric-motor-pumps depend on AC generation, and EPS uses a single generator part number across four positions (SDD §5.5.3) — a generic AC-generation common-mode reduces the C supply's diversity from B's engine-driven pumps under a total-AC scenario. Installation-Design / Environment (wing co-location), Common Resource (AC generation for HYD C).
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm and substantiate the separate routing of HYD C from A/B is maintained through the wing to the aileron actuators; capture the aileron actuation/surface mechanical common failure as a repeated/common-cause event feeding both channel branches; require zonal separation of the B-fed and C-fed aileron actuators at each surface; ensure HYD C RAT backstop covers the total-AC-generation common-mode.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• HYD C supply routing to the aileron actuators shall be physically separated from HYD B routing throughout the wing.
• The mechanical failure of aileron actuation/surface common to both hydraulic channels shall be modelled as a common-cause contributor to the effector-loss gate.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence between the HYD B aileron supply and the HYD C aileron supply.
aiRequirements: HYD C supply routing to the aileron actuators shall be physically separated from HYD B routing throughout the wing.
The mechanical failure of aileron actuation/surface common to both hydraulic channels shall be modelled as a common-cause contributor to the effector-loss gate.

cmaData.subject: G-028 independence — loss of roll command path (all three dissimilar FCS computers)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence across the three dissimilar flight control computers' roll command outputs.. Loss of the roll command path requires all three flight control computers (FCC 1, 2, 3) to fail, which are claimed independent through dissimilarity, separate bays and separate electrical sources.
cmaData.findings: Development phase (supports PSSA). The dissimilarity argument is strong on several axes: three dissimilar FCCs voting, software from two teams under a dissimilarity argument, each supplied from a different electrical source, installed in three separate bays — forward (zone 120), mid (zone 300), aft (zone 400) equipment bays (SDD §5.3.2/§5.3.5). Residual common causes: (1) Common air-data/inertial input — all three consume ADIRU air/inertial data; erroneous common-source data or a defeated voting/comparator is a common-mode across the set (already visible as the software/voting concern in the tree). (2) Common design/tools — only two software teams for three computers means at least two units may share a software baseline, reducing the pairwise diversity to a two-of-three dissimilarity. (3) Electrical: three different sources, but all trace to the same four-generator EPS with a single generator part number across positions (SDD §5.5.3), a design-level common-mode under progressive power loss. (4) Environment: FCC 2 sits in zone 300, the convergence zone for the majority of zone-spanning routings — a zone 300 event (fire, HV/LV crossing, hydraulic/bleed convergence) is a particular-risk/zonal candidate, but the other two FCCs are in 120/400, so no single zone takes all three. Development/Design (2 teams for 3 units, common air-data), Common Resource (EPS generation, ADIRU data).
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the three-of-three loss to carry an explicit common-cause contributor for shared air-data/inertial input and for defeated voting; substantiate that the two-team software split places no more than the tolerable number of units on a common baseline; verify the three electrical sources provide genuine segregation despite common generator part number (staggered overhaul already noted SDD §5.5.3); retain the mechanical reversion path to lower rudder/stab trim as the architectural backstop for total FCC loss.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The roll-command loss gate shall include a common-cause contributor representing shared air-data/inertial source error and defeated command voting.
• The software dissimilarity allocation across the three FCCs shall ensure no single software fault can disable more than the number of channels permitted by the independence claim.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence across the three dissimilar flight control computers' roll command outputs.
aiRequirements: The roll-command loss gate shall include a common-cause contributor representing shared air-data/inertial source error and defeated command voting.
The software dissimilarity allocation across the three FCCs shall ensure no single software fault can disable more than the number of channels permitted by the independence claim.

cmaData.subject: G-029 Complete loss of roll control authority — three-way independence of aileron, spoiler and FCC command legs
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three parallel roll-authority legs feeding the AND gate at node 66.. The aileron roll effectors, the multi-function spoiler roll path and the 3-FCC roll command path fail independently (node 66 AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / Installation-Design: aileron actuation depends on HYD B and HYD C (ailerons on B and C), spoiler on hydraulic supply, so the two effector legs are NOT hydraulically disjoint from each other — HYD B and HYD A share a wing-root run (zones 530/300/540) and all three surface legs converge with the command path in zone 300, the declared convergence zone for the majority of zone-spanning routings. A particular risk or zonal event in zone 300 (mid equipment bay / mid hold) can strike FCC 2 and the co-located hydraulic/data routings simultaneously, coupling the command leg to the effector legs. Development/Design: the three FCCs share a common command-voting architecture and common air-data/inertial input set.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain the zone-300 convergence and HYD A/B shared wing-root run as dedicated zonal (ZSA) and particular-risk items; verify minimum separation of FCC 2 from the shared routings; confirm no single zone-300 event fails more than one leg.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The installation shall ensure no single event in zone 300 simultaneously disables FCC 2 and either the aileron or spoiler hydraulic supply.
• The aileron and multi-function spoiler roll paths shall not share a single hydraulic system such that one hydraulic loss removes both effector legs.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ZSA of zone 300 and dedicated zonal item on the HYD A/B wing-root shared run; confirm the node-66 AND legs remain independent as installed (ASA).
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three parallel roll-authority legs feeding the AND gate at node 66.
aiRequirements: The installation shall ensure no single event in zone 300 simultaneously disables FCC 2 and either the aileron or spoiler hydraulic supply.
The aileron and multi-function spoiler roll paths shall not share a single hydraulic system such that one hydraulic loss removes both effector legs.
cmaData.aiVerification: ZSA of zone 300 and dedicated zonal item on the HYD A/B wing-root shared run; confirm the node-66 AND legs remain independent as installed (ASA).

cmaData.subject: G-029 — HYD A/B shared wing-root run coupling the surface effector legs
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Physical independence of the hydraulic supplies to the two roll effector groups.. Loss of the aileron effector leg and loss of the spoiler effector leg are independent (node 66 sub-legs 67 and 75).
cmaData.findings: Installation-Design / Environment: SDD states systems A and B share a wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (zones 530/300/540), recorded as an installation item to be examined. A rupture, fire or thermal event in that shared run can degrade both A and B, defeating the assumed independence between hydraulic supplies underpinning the aileron (B/C) and spoiler legs. HYD C is routed separately (zones 400/300/200) and does not share this run.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the A/B wing-root shared run as an explicit common-cause contributor to node 66; verify separately clipped bundles and separation adequacy; carry as a zonal item per SDD.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Hydraulic systems A and B shall be routed and protected in the shared wing-root run such that a single localised event cannot depressurise both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Dedicated zonal item on the A/B wing-root run; PRA reconciliation for zone 530/300/540 events (ASA).
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Physical independence of the hydraulic supplies to the two roll effector groups.
aiRequirements: Hydraulic systems A and B shall be routed and protected in the shared wing-root run such that a single localised event cannot depressurise both.
cmaData.aiVerification: Dedicated zonal item on the A/B wing-root run; PRA reconciliation for zone 530/300/540 events (ASA).

cmaData.subject: G-034 Uncommanded pitch — erroneous pitch command survives three-computer vote
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three dissimilar FCCs in generating an erroneous pitch command that defeats the vote.. FCC 1, FCC 2 and FCC 3 independently produce erroneous pitch command output (node 94 AND).
cmaData.findings: Development/Design common cause: although the three FCCs are on three different electrical sources and hosted by two software teams under a dissimilarity argument, they share a common command-voting architecture and a COMMON air-data/inertial input set. A common-mode error in the shared input data or in the common voting/comparator specification can drive all three to the same erroneous pitch command, so the AND does not represent true independence. Installation-Design: FCCs are in three separate bays (zones 120/300/400), but zone 300 is the convergence zone for the majority of zone-spanning routings — a zone-300 event threatens FCC 2 plus co-located data/network routings feeding all three. This principle underpins the DAL-A allocation on this tree; a specification/common-input failure here invalidates any independence credit that rested on the three-way vote.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm dissimilarity argument covers the voting/comparator design and the common input path, not only host software; model a common-mode input/spec error as an explicit contributor; verify zone-300 separation of FCC 2 and the network channels.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS shall detect and reject a common-mode erroneous air-data/inertial input before it can drive a coincident pitch command on all three FCCs.
• The command-voting/comparator function shall be shown free of a common specification or design error across all three FCCs.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Review of the FCS dissimilarity argument against the shared input and voting design; ZSA of zone 300 for FCC 2 and network channels (SSA/ASA).
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three dissimilar FCCs in generating an erroneous pitch command that defeats the vote.
aiRequirements: The FCS shall detect and reject a common-mode erroneous air-data/inertial input before it can drive a coincident pitch command on all three FCCs.
The command-voting/comparator function shall be shown free of a common specification or design error across all three FCCs.
cmaData.aiVerification: Review of the FCS dissimilarity argument against the shared input and voting design; ZSA of zone 300 for FCC 2 and network channels (SSA/ASA).

cmaData.subject: G-036 Slow uncommanded pitch divergence — slow erroneous pitch command survives three-computer vote
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three dissimilar FCCs in generating a low-rate erroneous pitch command that both defeats the vote and stays below the detection threshold.. FCC 1, FCC 2 and FCC 3 independently produce a slow erroneous pitch command output below detection threshold (node 103 AND).
cmaData.findings: Development/Design common cause: the slow-onset case is more exposed to common-mode than the fast case because a shared low-rate input drift (common air-data/inertial input set) or a common voting/comparator blind spot to sub-threshold rates can bias all three FCCs identically without tripping the cross-monitor. The dissimilarity argument (two software teams, three electrical sources) does not by itself cover a common input path or a common detection-threshold design. Installation-Design: FCC 2 in zone 300, the convergence zone, shares the environment with the majority of zone-spanning routings. Note G-036's top event (node 101) also ANDs this command survival with a failure-to-annunciate leg (node 109) — that annunciation leg is outside node 103 and is addressed by its own claim.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the detection/monitor threshold design is not common across all three FCCs; model shared slow-drift input as an explicit common-cause contributor; confirm zone-300 environmental separation of FCC 2.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS monitors shall detect a slow (sub-nominal-rate) erroneous pitch command arising from a common input drift before it produces an uncommanded divergence.
• The detection-threshold logic shall be shown not to share a common blind spot to low-rate errors across all three FCCs.

cmaData.subject: G-038 pitch-divergence annunciation independence (nodes 110 alerting ch A / 111 alerting ch B / 112 pitch-attitude display) — AND gate node 109, page-1788106623526-437

cmaData.subject: G-043/G-045 elevator actuation independence — HYD A-side vs HYD C-side elevator drive (page-1788106623544-366, gates id114/115/118)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent hydraulic supply per elevator actuator side (A and C physically and functionally separate).. cmaData.subject: G-043/G-045 FCS command-path independence — three FCCs to elevator (page-1788106623544-366, gate id121)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Triple dissimilar FCC command path, three separate bays, dissimilar software and separate electrical sources.. The FCS command path to the elevator survives because three dissimilar flight control computers (FCC1/2/3) fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design: FCCs are dissimilar, software developed by two teams under a dissimilarity argument, each on a different electrical source (SDD §5.3.2) — favourable against common-mode design/software error. Preserve three-bay physical separation and the dissimilar-software argument (SDD §5.3.2/§5.3.5); zonal analysis (ZSA zone 300, zone 400) to confirm no single hold event or shared routing in zone 300 defeats two FCCs; confirm the three FCC electrical sources are genuinely diverse down to bus level.

• The three FCC command paths to the elevator shall retain three-way physical separation such that no single zonal event (particularly in zone 300 / zone 400) disables more than one FCC.

cmaData.subject: G-047 yaw slow-divergence non-annunciation independence — alerting channels + display + detection threshold (page-1788106623567-908, gate id133)

cmaData.findings: Common Resources: crew alerting runs on two independent processing channels (SDD §5.11.2) but the alerting/standby/essential loads and the DC essential bus are the aircraft's final electrical resort (SDD §5.5.2), so a DC-essential loss is a candidate common cause across alerting and the standby display of yaw state. Installation Design: display processing units and networks are separated (three bays, dual networks, SDD §5.11.2/§5.11.5); yaw-state presentation depends on ADIRU/air-data — a common erroneous-source concern that could also mask the low-rate divergence from detection. The 'rate-below-threshold' leg is a design characteristic (monitor sensitivity), independent of the alerting/display hardware — favourable.

Confirm the two alerting processing channels do not share a single electrical source with the display path relied on to reveal yaw state; ensure the standby/independent yaw-state indication does not depend solely on DC essential when alerting also does; set the FCS/monitor low-rate detection threshold so slow divergence is not simultaneously below detection and unannunciated.

• The two crew-alerting processing channels shall not share a single electrical source that also feeds the display path relied upon to reveal a slow yaw divergence.

The upper rudder segment (HYD A) and lower rudder segment (HYD B), plus mechanical reversion, are independent so simultaneous loss requires the AND of separate causes.

Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence

cmaData.subject: G-055/G-056 main-bogie left/right independence (ground support & flotation)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Physical separation of left and right main gear bays substantiates the left/right AND-gate independence for complete loss of ground support/flotation.. Left-side (3 bogies, zone 710) and right-side (3 bogies, zone 720) collapse are independent — the tree ANDs them so simultaneous loss requires both sides.
cmaData.findings: Left and right bogies are installed in separate zones (710 vs 720), so no routing or single-bay event couples them. A common structural-sizing deficiency, common manufacturing lot, or the semi-prepared-surface overload case is a shared root that can degrade both sides together and defeat the left/right AND. Table M2 — | Common design of all six bogies / 20 tyres | shared sizing or lot deficiency degrades both sides | separate zones mitigate physical CCF but not design/manufacturing CCF | | Semi-prepared-surface overload (sizing case not frozen) | overloads both sides simultaneously | flotation/tyre sizing derived from a tactical airlifter — preliminary |
cmaData.mitigation:
Substantiate bogie/tyre structural sizing and flotation against the semi-prepared-surface case before the count is frozen; apply manufacturing lot/source diversity or lot traceability across the six bogies; carry the un-frozen leg count as an open item feeding PRA (tyre burst) and structural analysis.

• The main gear structural and flotation sizing shall be substantiated against the semi-prepared-surface overload case such that a common design condition does not defeat the left/right independence claimed at G-055.
• Manufacturing lot/source controls shall be applied across the six main bogies to limit common-lot common-cause failure.

cmaData.subject: G-060 brake hydraulic A/B co-location in main gear bays
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: HYD A and HYD B independence substantiates the normal/alternate AND-gate for complete loss of wheel braking.. Normal braking (HYD B) and alternate braking (HYD A) are independent, so the tree ANDs their loss with the accumulator leg.
cmaData.findings: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through EACH main gear bay in adjacent bundles that share the bay (zones 710/720), separately clipped and shielded. This is an Installation-Design / Environment common cause: a single bay event — tyre burst / flailing tread (PRA-54830), overheat (bay overheat detection is fitted), or a bay fire — can strike both the A and B brake lines together, defeating the normal/alternate AND. The fault tree does not currently model this co-location as a repeated event or common-cause gate. cmaData.subject: G-062 — Not-fully-closed condition not detected before flight (SF-010-M2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two detection paths that must both fail for a not-fully-closed visor to go undetected (AND gate node 175).. The SDD states lock status 'is included in the take-off configuration check' — the automated door-position indication and the crew check share the SAME take-off-configuration monitor path and are exercised by a SINGLE procedural step, so one TCM processing fault or one omitted/mis-performed config check defeats both inputs at once. Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The door-position detection presented to the crew and the automated take-off-configuration inhibit shall be sourced from independent sensing channels with no shared processing element.
• The take-off configuration procedure shall provide a detection of a not-fully-closed visor that does not rely solely on the same crew check that acknowledges the indication.

cmaData.subject: G-065 — Both dissimilar lock-sensing paths erroneously confirm locked (SF-011-M)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness node 183, mechanical linkage/visual indicator node 184).. The proximity sensing harness and the mechanical-linkage visual indicator independently confirm lock state, so both erroneously confirming locked requires two independent failures (AND gate node 182).
cmaData.findings: Strong claim, well supported: the two paths are dissimilar, independently routed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage, and cross the flight-deck bulkhead at two separated penetrations (SDD §5.7.2/§5.7.5) — this defeats Installation-Design and single-harness common cause. RESIDUAL common cause (already modelled as node 185): both paths read the SAME eight locking pins as their upstream reference, so a common mechanical reference error (pins report engaged while short-driven) and a common maintenance/calibration action can bias both paths the same way. Development-common-cause is low because the paths are dissimilar in kind (electrical proximity vs mechanical linkage).

Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The common upstream reference (locking-pin position) read by both dissimilar lock-sensing paths shall be shown not to introduce a single mechanical error that biases both paths to 'locked'.
• Maintenance and calibration of the two lock-sensing paths shall use dissimilar procedures / independent actions to preclude a common maintenance-induced error confirming a false locked state.

cmaData.subject: G-086 independence — erroneous reference/air-data source vs ADIRU comparison/voting (page-1788106623738-416, node 237)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of source error from voting/comparison rejection (AND: corrupted source AND voting fails to reject). An erroneous reference/air-data source and the failure of ADIRU comparison/voting to reject it fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Common Design — three air data inertial reference units are of a common type (SDD §5.11.2 'Three air data inertial reference units'); a common-mode air-data/inertial error affecting like units in the same way is the recognised failure that defeats comparison/voting (the tree already names this at node 227 'Common-mode air-data / inertial error'), confirming source error and voting are NOT independent for common-mode inputs. Common Resource — sensing: verify whether the three ADIRUs draw on shared or physically distinct pitot/static/AoA installations; a common probe error (e.g. common icing/blockage) is a shared cause reaching multiple units simultaneously (PRA-54836 icing / probe heat SF-017 relevance). Common Resource — supply: two ADIRUs on main buses, one on DC essential (SDD §5.11.2); not a full common-cause but note the essential-bus dependency. Development/Software — voting/comparison logic is a single algorithm; a specification or software defect in the comparison function is a common cause with the source data it is meant to reject.
cmaData.mitigation:
Represent common-mode air-data/inertial error explicitly as a common-cause contributor (as already begun at node 227) rather than relying on the AND. Confirm probe/sensing dissimilarity or independent probe heat so a single icing/blockage event does not corrupt the units voting sees as agreeing. Cross-check probe-heat / icing (SF-017, PRA-54836) as the shared environmental cause behind common source error.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The air-data/inertial sources feeding the primary display chain shall be sufficiently dissimilar or independently sensed that a single common cause cannot corrupt enough sources to defeat comparison/voting.
• The comparison/voting function shall be developed to a dissimilarity or integrity standard such that its failure to reject is not correlated with the source error it must detect.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Verification-phase (ASA/SSA): verify ADIRU sensing independence (probe installation and heating) and the voting/comparison implementation against the common-mode air-data/inertial error path (node 227); confirm whether the G-086 AND independence holds or a common-cause contributor is required. This principle underpins any DAL reduction resting on triplex voting (App P) — if common-mode source error defeats voting, that reduction is invalid.

cmaData.subject: G-087 network channels 1 & 2 delivering corrupted flight/nav parameters — AND-gate independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual redundant deterministic data network, channels routed on opposite sides sharing no connector or penetration.. The two data network channels fail independently, so both delivering corrupted parameters requires two independent faults.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (data/processing): both channels feed the same three display processing units and derive from the same ADIRU set — a common-source data corruption upstream of the split (node 227/238 common-mode air-data/inertial error) defeats the channel-pair AND, since identical corrupted parameters would be delivered on both channels. Development/Design (software/hardware): the deterministic network protocol and end-system hardware are of common design across both channels; a common protocol/端-system defect corrupts both identically. Installation Design / Environment: SDD states channels are opposite-side with no shared connector or penetration, which addresses physical co-location and EMI common cause. Common Resources (electrical): both channels ultimately serve DC/AC-fed display processors; a shared supply upstream is a candidate.
cmaData.mitigation:
Opposite-side routing with no shared connector/penetration (SDD §5.11.5/§4) mitigates physical/EMI common cause. NOT assured against: common network protocol/end-system design defect and common upstream ADIRU source corruption — these belong in the tree as a common-cause contributor above the channel AND (the tree already models common-mode source error at node 227/238; verify it is not double-defeated at the channel level). Independence requirement (dev): the two channels shall use dissimilar or independently-verified protocol/端-system implementations, or the DAL credit for the channel-pair AND shall not rest on independence; upstream source-data integrity monitoring shall be independent of the channel that carries it. Where this AND underpins a DAL reduction per App P, a common protocol defect invalidates that reduction.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA (verification phase): confirm as-built channel end-systems and protocol stacks are dissimilar or independently substantiated; confirm no shared power feed to the two channel end-systems; confirm ADIRU comparison/voting (node 239) is not implemented on a resource common to both channels.

cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA (verification phase): confirm as-built channel end-systems and protocol stacks are dissimilar or independently substantiated; confirm no shared power feed to the two channel end-systems; confirm ADIRU comparison/voting (node 239) is not implemented on a resource common to both channels.

cmaData.subject: G-090 primary display path AND independent standby both present misleading flight/nav information — top AND-gate independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent integrated standby instrument sharing no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays.. The primary display chain and the independent standby instrument fail independently, so misleading information reaching the crew undetected requires both to be wrong.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (electrical): the standby instrument is on the DC essential bus; one of the three ADIRUs is also on the DC essential bus (SDD §5.11.2) — a DC-essential-bus failure removes the standby (node 246) and could correlate with primary-side effects, a candidate coupling to test. Common Resources (sensors): standby uses independent pitot/static/attitude sensing; if that sensing shares a probe-heat resource or a static source region with the primary system, a common icing/blockage event could mislead both — cross-reference the icing PRA and probe-heat function. Development/Design: standby is an integrated instrument of different design from the primary display chain — dissimilarity supports the independence claim (node 234/244). Installation: standby wired directly to DC essential on a route independent of the primary display feeders (SDD §5.11.5) mitigates routing/connector common cause. Environment (EMI/HIRF): a HIRF/lightning event enveloping the flight deck could affect both display domains — reconcile with the HIRF/lightning PRA.
cmaData.mitigation:
Design dissimilarity and independent supply/sensor/processing (SDD §5.11.3) substantiate the AND for random and design-common-mode. NOT assured against: shared static-source / probe-heat common cause misleading both channels identically, and a common flight-deck HIRF/lightning environment. Independence requirement (dev): the standby sensing shall not share a probe, static port or probe-heat channel with the primary air-data path relied on in this AND; confirm the DC-essential-bus ADIRU cannot introduce a common misleading source into both the primary path and any standby cross-check. Where this top AND supports the Catastrophic classification of SF-018-M, a shared static/probe-heat source or HIRF susceptibility that defeats it must be surfaced as a common-cause contributor.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA (verification phase): confirm as-built the standby instrument shares no static source, no probe-heat channel and no processing with the primary displays; confirm DC-essential-bus loss behaviour of standby is annunciated; confirm HIRF/lightning qualification covers simultaneous exposure of primary and standby domains.

cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA (verification phase): confirm as-built the standby instrument shares no static source, no probe-heat channel and no processing with the primary displays; confirm DC-essential-bus loss behaviour of standby is annunciated; confirm HIRF/lightning qualification covers simultaneous exposure of primary and standby domains.

cmaData.subject: G-091 both alerting processing channels lost — AND-gate independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Alerting consolidation driven by two independent processing channels; presentation via display units and head-up displays.. The two alerting processing channels fail independently, so complete loss of alerting requires both channels plus the presentation path to fail.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources (electrical): both alerting channels and the presentation path ultimately depend on electrical supply — node 254 already models 'loss of electrical supply to both alerting' as a shared contributor, correctly surfaced. Verify the two channels are on genuinely different sources (the SDD asserts alerting is on the DC essential bus for fire/overheat detection §5.12.4, and DC essential is the 'final electrical resort' §5.5.2 hosting many consumers) — DC-essential dependence is a candidate common resource that could defeat the channel-pair AND. Common Resources (processing/data): both channels consolidate from the same source system status feeds and run on the display/network infrastructure; a common data-network or display-processing failure (node 252) can remove presentation for both channels — the tree models this as a parallel AND leg, verify it is not itself a single point. Development/Design (software): the two processing channels — if common-design software — share a systematic defect; the SDD does not state alerting-channel dissimilarity (unlike the FCS §5.3.2), so a common software defect is a credible un-mitigated contributor. Installation: channel co-location not stated for alerting; retain as item.
cmaData.mitigation:
Shared electrical supply is already modelled (node 254) and presentation-path loss is a separate AND leg (node 251) — good. NOT assured against: common alerting-channel software defect (no dissimilarity claimed in the SDD) and common DC-essential-bus dependence of both channels. Independence requirement (dev): the two alerting processing channels shall be supplied from different electrical sources and shall not both depend solely on the DC essential bus; the alerting-channel software shall be dissimilar or independently verified, or the AND-gate independence credit shall be withdrawn. Where this AND underpins the Catastrophic SF-019-TL objective and any App P DAL reduction, a common software defect or common DC-essential dependence invalidates that reduction.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA (verification phase): confirm as-built the two alerting channels are on different power sources (not both DC essential only); confirm alerting-channel software dissimilarity or independent verification evidence; confirm the presentation-path AND (node 251) has no single display-processing resource that removes both DU and HUD annunciation.

cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA (verification phase): confirm as-built the two alerting channels are on different power sources (not both DC essential only); confirm alerting-channel software dissimilarity or independent verification evidence; confirm the presentation-path AND (node 251) has no single display-processing resource that removes both DU and HUD annunciation.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Redundant alert-presentation surfaces (4 DUs + 2 HUDs) are independent so no single cause removes all crew-alert presentation.. The display units and head-up displays that present crew alerts fail independently (AND-gate independence at node 251).
cmaData.findings: Common Resource: the presentation surfaces are driven by three shared display processing units on a shared dual-redundant data network — a common-source corruption or a display-processing/network fault is a common cause across the presentation set, defeating the AND. Development/Design: DUs are of a common type/format engine ('any display unit can present any format'), a common-design contributor. Phase: development (PSSA).

Independence requirement (dev): alert presentation shall retain at least one annunciation path not dependent on the three display processing units or the primary data network (e.g. a dedicated aural/discrete master-warning path), and the display-processing/network common-mode shall be surfaced as a repeated event or common-cause gate under node 251 rather than left as a pure AND. cmaData.subject: G-096 — Both detection loops lost in an engine nacelle (610–640): loop independence within the nacelle fire zone
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual continuous detection loops, routed separately with AND logic, are independent so no single cause loses detection in a nacelle.. The two nacelle fire-detection loops fail independently (AND-gate independence at node 262).
cmaData.findings: Installation-Design / Environment: both loops reside inside a single engine nacelle (zone 610/620/630/640), a high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone; the fire/overheat particular risk and the nacelle thermal/mechanical environment that the loops exist to detect are themselves a common cause capable of disabling both loops — a same-zone AND must carry this. Development/Design: the two loops are the same continuous-loop type, a common-design/common-type contributor. Note the SDD mitigates conductor-level co-location by routing the two loops on opposite sides of the zone and separately clipping them, which addresses local damage but not the whole-zone environmental threat. Phase: development (PSSA).
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirement (dev): the same-zone environmental/particular-risk common cause (nacelle fire, rotor-burst/engine-burst debris per §25.903(d)(1)/§25.901(c), thermal) shall be carried under node 262 as a common-cause contributor rather than left as a pure AND; loop routing/dissimilarity shall be substantiated against the nacelle zonal and particular-risk analyses. Verification note (SSA/ASA): reconcile with the nacelle ZSA and rotor-/engine-burst PRA that a single zonal event does not defeat both loops before it is itself detected.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: reconcile node 262 independence with nacelle ZSA and rotor/engine-burst PRA; confirm opposite-side routing and separate clipping as built.

The two continuous fire/overheat detection loops in each engine nacelle fail independently, so simultaneous loss requires both loops to fail from unrelated causes.

Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1) Common design/type — both loops are the same continuous-detection technology | A design or calibration error common to the type defeats both loops together | LACK OF INDEPENDENCE: no dissimilarity stated between the two loops; degraded single-loop logic does not protect against a common-type latent fault
