cmaData.subject: G-104 Both oxygen cylinder sources unavailable — two-cylinder independence (SF-022-TL, page "No breathing oxygen delivered to crew masks on demand")
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Common Resources (stored gaseous O2 sources) | Common Design/Type | Installation-Design co-location | Maintenance/servicing. The two high-pressure oxygen cylinders fail independently, so loss of both stored sources is the product of two independent events.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Co-location — both cylinders installed in zone 120 forward equipment bay; a single zonal event (bay fire, impact) can disable both, defeating the AND. | Lack of independence — no zonal separation stated. :: (2) Common design/type — two like gaseous cylinders of common specification and common overpressure/relief design; a common material/charge or overpressure-vent defect affects both (thermal discharge indicator shows overboard vent of a cylinder overpressure). | Common design common cause; part-number commonality vs dissimilarity not stated in SDD. :: (3) Common maintenance/servicing — cylinder pressure is a single dispatch check; both charged/serviced by one action, a common mis-charge / under-fill human-error path. | Common maintenance error; staggered servicing not stated. :: (4) Undetected common depletion — SF-022-PL3 undetected loss of stored quantity is an unaware condition; a slow common leak can deplete both sources with no crew alert, so the AND does not protect against gradual common loss. | Lack of independence in the detection path.
cmaData.mitigation: Separate the two cylinders zonally or provide protection so a single zone-120 event cannot take both; confirm and record cylinder part-number / lot dissimilarity or add a mitigating manufacturing-lot control; apply staggered servicing / independent pressure verification per cylinder; provide stored-quantity monitoring that alerts on slow depletion (closes SF-022-PL3). hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect total thrust loss from engine parameter indication and deceleration/aural cues, identify an all-engine loss condition, and establish and manage a glide toward a forced-landing option.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-001-TL · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect asymmetric thrust from yaw/heading deviation and engine indication, identify the affected side, and apply rudder and asymmetry compensation to hold directional control.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-001-M · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect uncommanded reverser deployment from thrust/deceleration cues and reverser indication, identify the affected reverser, and command it stowed while retarding the associated thrust lever.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-002-M · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed no discrete crew recovery restores roll control, so the crew carry the condition without a credited corrective action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-003-TL · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect a wrong-sense or excessive pitch response from attitude and rate cues against their commanded input, identify the erroneous response, and counter it with pitch input as available.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew recognise an uncommanded pitch excursion from attitude and rate indication and override it with opposing pitch input using the available authority.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M2 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot detect a pitch divergence developing below the detection threshold, so no corrective action is credited for this condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-M3 · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect the reduced available pitch range from attitude and control-position cues, identify the narrower authority, and hold pitch within the remaining range.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-PL · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed no crew pitch input remains available, so no credited corrective action arrests the pitch divergence.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-TL · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect the pitch-authority shortfall from response and rate cues, identify the reduced envelope, and fly within it while managing gust and configuration demands.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-004-PL2 · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed no effective crew means of directional control remains, so no credited corrective action maintains heading or track.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-TL · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot detect yaw-authority degradation developing below the detection threshold, so no corrective action is credited until a directional demand reveals the shortfall.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-PL3 · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot detect a yaw divergence developing below the detection threshold, so no corrective action is credited for this condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-005-M3 · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect uncommanded gear movement from gear-position indication and configuration cues, identify the unexpected configuration change, and respond per the applicable procedure.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-007-M2 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew cannot detect asymmetric braking developing below the detection threshold, so no corrective action is credited for this condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-008-M4 · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect reduced braking effectiveness from deceleration cues, identify the shortfall during the ground roll, and apply maximum braking, available inboard reverse thrust and directional control.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-008-PL · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect loss of anti-skid from wheel-lockup and deceleration cues, identify the degraded protection, and modulate braking manually to avoid lock-up during the ground roll.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-008-PL2 · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect the braking asymmetry from tracking deviation, identify the affected wheel pair, and correct with steering, rudder and differential braking while applying reverse thrust.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-008-PL3 · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew perceive an abnormally long ground roll from deceleration and runway-position cues, identify reduced braking effectiveness late, and take corrective braking and deceleration action.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-008-PL4 · framed per HIDH §5.7.5.1 time-occupancy Red Line (Parks & Boucek 1989)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect loss of nose-wheel steering from tracking response, identify the failure, and maintain runway/taxiway tracking using differential braking and rudder.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-009-TL · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect reduced steering authority from tracking response and correct ground tracking with additional steering and rudder input.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-009-PL · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect an uncommanded steering deflection from tracking deviation, identify the uncommanded input, and counter rapidly with differential braking and rudder.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-009-M · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew detect an erroneous, counter-intuitive steering response from tracking deviation against their command, identify the erroneous response, and counter with differential braking and rudder.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-009-M2 · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew read flight-deck lock-status indication, identify a change in door lock state, and act on it within the take-off configuration check.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-010-M · framed per HIDH §5.7.4.2.2 multiple-resource task decomposition

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the crew are given no valid cue because lock-secure confirmation is erroneous, so no crew detection or corrective action is credited for this condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-011-M3 · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew read the remaining dissimilar lock-sensing indication, identify the retained lock state, and confirm it within the take-off configuration check.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-011-PL · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew read the surviving dissimilar lock-sensing indication, identify the retained lock state, and confirm it within the take-off configuration check.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-011-PL2 · framed per HIDH §5.7 cognitive workload

hfaRows.text: It is assumed that, where the loss is annunciated, the flight crew read the loss-of-lock-confirmation indication, identify the absence of valid confirmation, and refuse pressurised dispatch; where the unconfirmed state is undetected, no cue is available and no action is credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-011-TL · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed that, absent a tension-monitoring annunciation, the crew are given no cue to the restraint shortfall, so no detection or corrective action is credited for this condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-012-M · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew read the restraint-condition annunciation and identify the loss of restraint, but no in-flight corrective action is available, so no recovery is credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-012-TL · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew read the loss-of-tension annunciation and identify the reduced-restraint condition, but with indication only and no in-flight adjustment no recovery action is credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-012-PL · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)

hfaRows.text: It is assumed the flight crew read the loss-of-tension annunciation and identify the below-required tension condition, but with indication only and no in-flight adjustment no recovery action is credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI · HFA draft from SF-012-PL2 · framed per HFA register posture (credited vs uncredited)
